B.contract: Registered unstructure hooks and private-attribute handling must apply at every nesting level; the top-level instance used the cattrs hook while nested instances of the same class produced different output.

C.label: bug
C.description: Hooks for recursive classes generated during the probe used to_builtins and ignored cattrs hooks, giving wrong output.
C.contract: Nested recursive private fields must go through cattrs hooks.

B.label: feature
B.description: register_structure_hook and register_unstructure_hook gain a dedicated branch for PEP 695 type aliases, which before the commit fell through to singledispatch and were rejected with 'Invalid first argument to register() ... is not a class or union type'.
B.contract: No prior promise covered this entry point: both docstrings add 'versionchanged:: 25.1.0 Modern type aliases are now supported', the old rejection was a clean argument-type check rather than a crash in cattrs logic, and type-alias support already existed elsewhere in the converter (pre-existing test_type_aliases), so the failing test exercises a newly accepted input to the simple register_*_hook API.

C.label: feature
C.description: register_structure_hook and register_unstructure_hook gain support for PEP 695 type aliases, which they previously rejected with a TypeError.
C.contract: The docstrings gain 'versionchanged 25.1.0: Modern type aliases are now supported'; the tests fail only because the registration path for aliases did not exist.

B.label: bug
B.description: make_hetero_tuple_structure_fn interpolated str(cl) unescaped into a single-quoted string literal in generated source, so a type whose repr contains a quote (e.g. Literal['a']) made compiling the hook raise SyntaxError.
B.contract: Structuring Tuple[Literal['a'], int] or a NamedTuple with a Literal field is valid input that BaseConverter and Converter(detailed_validation=False) handle; only the generated detailed-validation path crashed.

C.label: bug
C.description: Quotes in type reprs were interpolated unescaped into generated source, causing SyntaxError.
C.contract: Hetero tuple structuring must compile for types like Literal["a"].

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: BaseConverter registers the attrs-union disambiguation hook only for the AS_DICT unstructure strategy, so structuring such a union with an AS_TUPLE converter raises StructureHandlerNotFoundError instead of ValueError('Only input mappings are supported').
B.contract: The ValueError for tuple-strategy unions was the tested, expected behaviour (old tests used pytest.raises(ValueError) under the comment 'Our disambiguation functions only support dictionaries for now'), and this test-dependency bump updates those tests to the new exception type, so the change alters error behaviour for an unsupported case rather than fixing a fault.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: The BaseConverter only registers the supported-union disambiguation structure hook for the AS_DICT strategy, so tuple-strategy unions now raise StructureHandlerNotFoundError instead of ValueError.
C.contract: Mostly a test-dependency bump; the source change alters the error raised for unsupported tuple-strategy unions and the tests were rewritten to expect it.

B.label: bug
B.description: make_dict_unstructure_fn read per-attribute overrides with kwargs.pop while generating code, which emptied the overrides mapping later exposed as the generated function's .overrides, so callers saw {} instead of the overrides they passed.
B.contract: Generated hooks expose the overrides they were built with: the existing test_renaming already asserted that s_fn.overrides equals the passed overrides for the structure function, and the commit message 'Fix keeping unstructuring overrides' states that the unstructure function must keep them as well.

C.label: bug
C.description: make_dict_unstructure_fn consumed the overrides with kwargs.pop(), so the generated function's overrides mapping came out empty, and the fix uses kwargs.get().
C.contract: The structure counterpart already exposes its overrides mapping, and the test asserts that u_fn.overrides equals the overrides passed in; the message says 'Fix keeping unstructuring overrides', so the loss of overrides was a defect.

B.label: bug
B.description: The include_subclasses union-strategy path called __subclasses__() and issubclass() directly on a parameterised generic parent such as GenericParent[Any], raising AttributeError, instead of first unwrapping the alias with typing.get_origin.
B.contract: Generic parents were already supported by include_subclasses (existing test_parents_with_generics), so crashing when the same parent is combined with configure_tagged_union is a crash on valid input; the commit is titled 'Fix include_subclasses strategy with a generic parent and tagged_union' and its test references issue #682.

C.label: bug
C.description: include_subclasses with a generic parent and tagged union called __subclasses__ and issubclass on parametrized generic aliases, raising AttributeError.
C.contract: Commit is a fix backport for issue #682; generic parents were already supported by include_subclasses, and the crash is on valid input.

B.label: feature
B.description: Generated attrs dict (un)structure hooks additionally record an override with rename set to the alias in their overrides metadata whenever _cattrs_use_alias maps an attribute to a different key.
B.contract: The alias keys were already applied by the generated code (the key computation is unchanged context in the diff, so the round-trip assertions exercise old logic), the fail-to-pass tests fail only on the new metadata lookup (KeyError 'a' on fn.overrides), and the title 'Generate rename metadata for aliases' describes added introspection data rather than a broken promise.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Generated hooks now record the alias as rename metadata in the overrides when _cattrs_use_alias is set.
C.contract: Tests fail on inspecting the overrides' rename attribute (KeyError); serialized output with aliases already worked, so this exposes metadata rather than fixing a wrong result.

B.label: feature
B.description: Enums whose _value_ attribute is annotated get their values unstructured and structured through the annotated type (for example tuples of other enums) via a new _structure_enum hook and an extended _unstructure_enum.
B.contract: Enums were previously implemented and described as converting to and from their raw value ('Convert an enum to its value.'); the commit calls itself 'an initial implementation' with new docs and history, and the tests fail only because complex-value support did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds structuring and unstructuring of enums whose values are complex types, driven by a _value_ annotation.
C.contract: Commit says 'initial implementation' with docs; the capability did not exist before.

B.label: bug
B.description: GenConverter overrode the public unstructure_attrs_asdict with a version that registered a generated hook, so calling it from a user's manual hook replaced that manual hook and later unstructuring lost the custom output.
B.contract: Calling the public helper from a hook must not replace user-registered hooks (issue 118); the test checks repeated unstructuring keeps the type tag.

C.label: bug
C.description: Calling unstructure_attrs_asdict from a hook overrode the user hook by registering a generated one.
C.contract: Manual hook must not be overwritten

B.label: bug
B.description: The default union disambiguator collected literal discriminator fields by attribute name and ignored rename overrides, so structuring a union whose literal fields were renamed looked up the attribute name in the payload and raised KeyError or failed to disambiguate.
B.contract: create_default_dis_func already accepted per-class overrides and honoured renames for key-based disambiguation (existing test_field_renaming); payloads produced by hooks with renamed literal fields could not be structured back through the union.

C.label: bug
C.description: Union disambiguation used original names for literal fields, ignoring rename overrides.
C.contract: Renamed fields should be honored in disambiguation (KeyError otherwise).

B.label: bug
B.description: format_exception joined the ForbiddenExtraKeysError.extra_fields set directly, so transform_error listed multiple extra keys in hash-randomized, run-dependent order.
B.contract: ForbiddenExtraKeysError.__str__ already sorted the same set, so the two renderings of one error disagreed; the same input should yield a stable transform_error result.

C.label: bug
C.description: Extra keys were joined from a set so error messages had nondeterministic order.
C.contract: transform_error output should be stable across runs.

B.label: feature
B.description: The converters gain hooks that evaluate Python 3.14 annotationlib.ForwardRef objects produced by PEP 649 deferred annotations, so self-referential attrs classes and dataclasses round-trip instead of leaving nested instances unconverted.
B.contract: This adds support for an annotation object introduced by Python 3.14's deferred-evaluation semantics: the commit is titled 'Support `annotationlib.ForwardRef`', the tests live in a new PEP 649 test module, and the packet shows no earlier promise covering these objects.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds handling of annotationlib.ForwardRef (PEP 649 / Python 3.14 deferred annotations) in structure/unstructure hook dispatch.
C.contract: Commit title 'Support annotationlib.ForwardRef'; adds support for a new Python annotation mechanism with new hooks and tests.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: The default structure_fallback_factory raises StructureHandlerNotFoundError as soon as a hook is requested for an unsupported type, instead of returning raise_error so that the failure only happens when structuring runs, and find_structure_handler is adapted to catch the exception.
B.contract: Returning raise_error lazily was the established default since structure_fallback_factory was added in 23.2.0; the commit adds 'versionchanged:: 24.2.0 The default structure_fallback_factory now raises errors for missing handlers more eagerly' and keeps the legacy raise_error comparison working, so the test checks a new default rather than a repaired fault.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: The default structure fallback factory now raises StructureHandlerNotFoundError when the hook is looked up, instead of returning a hook that raises only when it is called.
C.contract: A versionchanged note 24.2.0 documents it as a deliberate change ('raises errors for missing handlers more eagerly'); lazy failure was the earlier intended design, not a fault.

B.label: bug
B.description: _make_subclasses_tree called __subclasses__() directly on the class given to include_subclasses, so a parameterized generic parent such as GenericParent[str] (a typing alias that has no __subclasses__) crashed with AttributeError instead of being unwrapped to its origin class.
B.contract: cattrs treats parameterized generic attrs classes as ordinary attrs classes (structuring GenericParent[str] is supported), and include_subclasses signals genuinely unsupported classes with StructureHandlerNotFoundError (existing test_unsupported_class), so a raw internal AttributeError on a valid generic attrs parent is a crash on valid input; the commit resolves issue #648 and its body calls the change a fix, although the title words it as 'Support generic parents'.

C.label: bug
C.description: include_subclasses called __subclasses__() directly on a parametrized generic alias such as GenericParent[str], raising AttributeError instead of using the alias's origin class.
C.contract: include_subclasses is expected to work for any class that is a valid parent, including generic parents; the crash is an AttributeError on valid input (issue #648), and the test checks that the child is structured through GenericParent[str].

B.label: bug
B.description: The TypedDict hook generator wrapped key names in hand-written single quotes ('{attr_name}') without escaping, so a key containing an apostrophe produced syntactically invalid generated code and (un)structuring failed with SyntaxError.
B.contract: TypedDict keys may be arbitrary strings (functional syntax) and cattrs is expected to (un)structure any valid TypedDict, so a SyntaxError on a key containing an apostrophe is a crash on valid input; the commit message says it fixes handling keys with single quotes, and the fix switches to repr-based quoting ({attr_name!r}).

C.label: bug
C.description: Generated TypedDict hook code embedded keys inside hand-written single quotes, producing a SyntaxError for keys containing a single quote.
C.contract: Any valid TypedDict key should round-trip; generated code raising SyntaxError is a crash on valid input.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Under detailed validation, TypedDict structuring checks isinstance(o, Mapping) up front and raises TypeError('expected a mapping, not <type>'), so the transformed error for non-mapping input reads 'invalid type (expected a mapping, not int)' instead of 'expected a mapping'.
B.contract: The old message for the recorded failures ('expected a mapping @ $' and '@ $.c') was accurate and deliberately produced by a dedicated AttributeError branch in v.format_exception that the commit removes; the commit message says 'improve error message on invalid input' and the test edits update the expected text, with the added list-input case being a further improvement whose old output the packet does not show.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: The error message produced when a TypedDict is structured from a non-mapping is reworded from 'expected a mapping' to 'invalid type (expected a mapping, not int)', and the check is made with an explicit isinstance.
C.contract: The old message was correct, and the commit message says 'improve error message'; the tests only assert the new wording.

B.label: bug
B.description: StructureHandlerNotFoundError and ForbiddenExtraKeysError passed only a message to Exception.__init__, so their args did not match their constructor signatures and the errors could not be pickled and restored correctly.
B.contract: Exceptions are expected to survive a pickle round-trip (for example across process boundaries) and BaseException.args holds the constructor arguments used to rebuild them; the commit message says it 'correctly' sets args to make the errors picklable, and the new pickling test fails on the old, message-only args.

C.label: bug
C.description: Error classes passed only the message to super().__init__, so BaseException.args did not hold the constructor arguments and pickling/unpickling failed to round-trip.
C.contract: Exceptions are expected to be picklable with args equal to constructor args; the commit title says args were incorrectly set and made picklable.

B.label: feature
B.description: configure_union_passthrough is extended to resolve PEP 695 type aliases among union members, so an exact union such as NewScalar | DataClass (with type NewScalar = str) can be handled by the native passthrough.
B.contract: Nothing in the packet shows a prior promise that alias members work in passthrough unions; the commit is titled 'Support type aliases in union passthrough' and the new tests fail only with StructureHandlerNotFoundError because alias members were not recognised before the change.

C.label: feature
C.description: configure_union_passthrough is extended to resolve PEP 695 type aliases inside unions.
C.contract: Commit title says 'Support type aliases'; alias handling in passthrough was not an existing promise, though one could argue it is a gap.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: The msgpack and cbor2 converters change from unstructuring naive datetimes with datetime.timestamp(), which reads them as local time, to treating them as UTC before taking the timestamp.
B.contract: The old hook followed Python's standard naive-datetime semantics and nothing in the packet documents that naive datetimes were meant to be UTC; the commit title 'Assume naive datetimes are UTC' and the new docstrings present a newly chosen assumption for symmetry with the UTC structure hook, so this is a policy change rather than a repair of promised behaviour.

C.label: bug
C.description: msgpack/cbor2 unstructure hook used datetime.timestamp(), which treats naive datetimes as local time, so output depended on machine timezone and did not round-trip with the UTC structure hook.
C.contract: The structure hook reads timestamps as UTC, so round-trip consistency and machine-independent serialization are expected invariants.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The converters adopt UTC as the interpretation of naive datetimes, replacing the local-time interpretation supplied by datetime.timestamp().
T.contract: The packet establishes that timestamp decoding uses UTC, but that does not establish a prior promise to interpret naive inputs as UTC; the added tests enforce the newly selected timezone policy.

B.label: bug
B.description: The UsageError hint always used ctx.help_option_names[0], so it suggested '-h' even when a subcommand option shadowed '-h' and that flag would not show help.
B.contract: The hint must name a help option that actually works for the command (issue #2790); get_help_option_names already excludes shadowed names. Some failing cases also reflect the added prefer-longest-name policy, but the shadowed '-h' case checks the fault.

C.label: bug
C.description: Usage error hint used the first help name even when shadowed by another option.
C.contract: Hint must show a help option name that actually works.

B.label: bug
B.description: Help rendering compared an arbitrary default value to '' with ==, which raised for objects whose __eq__ rejects string operands (e.g. semver-like versions).
B.contract: Any object is a valid option default and get_help_record with show_default=True should render it via str(); issue #3298 reports the crash.

C.label: bug
C.description: Empty-string default check compared arbitrary objects with ==, raising for objects with strict __eq__.
C.contract: show_default must work for any default type.

B.label: bug
B.description: ProgressBar never applied the pending steps below update_min_steps at finish, so a length not divisible by the threshold left the bar short of completion (e.g. 14/20).
B.contract: A finished progress bar must show its full length; the test is a regression test for issue 3571.

C.label: bug
C.description: Progress bar left a sub-threshold remainder unapplied, freezing below the final position.
C.contract: Bar should end at its total

B.label: bug
B.description: click.Path.convert checked the dash sentinel with 'rv in (b"-", "-")', comparing str against bytes and raising BytesWarning (an error under python -bb).
B.contract: Converting an ordinary path value must not fail when Python runs with -bb; the test runs the conversion under -bb and expects a clean exit.

C.label: bug
C.description: Path dash detection compared bytes with str, emitting BytesWarning under python -bb.
C.contract: No BytesWarning on valid input

B.label: bug
B.description: FishComplete wrote completion help text containing literal newlines into its line-based 'type,value<TAB>help' output, so multi-line help strings split one completion into several broken entries.
B.contract: Options with multi-line help are valid and completion should not break on them (#3043); the commit fixes this by escaping newlines, but it also switches to a newline-separated format that most fail-to-pass tests pin and that a later commit reverts as a fish regression.

C.label: bug
C.description: Fish completion broke on multiline help strings.
C.contract: Completion must handle multiline help (issue 3043).

B.label: bug
B.description: prompt and confirm echoed all but the last prompt character themselves and passed only that last character to the readline-backed input function, so readline mis-tracked the line (backspace/wrapping) and with err=True the last character leaked to stdout.
B.contract: With err=True the whole prompt should go to stderr (issue #3019) and line editing should work under readline (issue #2968); the old output split the prompt across stdout and stderr.

C.label: bug
C.description: Prompt text was written separately, breaking readline backspace and line wrapping on Linux.
C.contract: Prompts should be passed fully to readline (issue 2969).

B.label: bug
B.description: HelpFormatter.write_usage with empty args passed an empty string to wrap_text, which returned '' and discarded the usage prefix, so the usage line was blank (or got a trailing space and extra newline when the program name was long).
B.contract: A command with no parameters and options_metavar='' or None should still render 'Usage: <prog>'; issue #3360 reports the blank usage line as a defect.

C.label: bug
C.description: write_usage with no args emitted a blank or spurious output instead of the usage prefix.
C.contract: Usage line should print just the prefix (issues 3360, 3434).

B.label: bug
B.description: lookup_default and the default resolution treated a default_map key holding the internal UNSET sentinel as an explicit value, so the parameter's own default was skipped and the value came out as None.
B.contract: UNSET is click's marker for 'no value supplied', so an UNSET entry should behave like an absent key and fall back to the parameter default (port=8000).

C.label: bug
C.description: The internal UNSET sentinel stored in default_map leaked as a real default value.
C.contract: UNSET must be treated as absent; test expects port=8000.

B.label: bug
B.description: Option.__init__ eagerly replaced default=True with flag_value, so when flag_value was a callable such as a class, the generic callable-default handling invoked it and the option yielded an instance instead of the class.
B.contract: default=True on a flag means 'activate the flag by default' and should give the same value as passing the flag (the class itself); issue #3121 reports the instantiation as a regression.

C.label: bug
C.description: Callable flag_value such as a class was instantiated when used as default.
C.contract: Callable flag_value must be preserved (issue 3121).

B.label: bug
B.description: get_pager_file treated any stream without a truthy encoding as binary, so a text-only StringIO (encoding None) was wrapped in MaybeStripAnsi as if it were a byte stream instead of being yielded as-is.
B.contract: The pre-fix code's own comment states that StringIO streams should only get a .color attribute and no wrapping; that branch was unreachable for real StringIO objects, so the no-stdout fallback stream was replaced by a text wrapper around a text stream.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: get_pager_file stream wrapping refactored with tests added; tests assert stream identity and flush behaviour.
C.contract: Followup that mainly adds tests and restructures stream handling.

T.label: bug
T.description: Pager stream detection misclassified StringIO as binary because it lacked an encoding, wrapping a text-only stream in a byte-oriented adapter.
T.contract: The existing pager API promises a writable text file-like object, and its text-stream fallback must remain usable when stdout is unavailable.

B.label: feature
B.description: click.prompt gains support for a string show_default that is displayed in parentheses, and Option forwards non-bool show_default values to the prompt.
B.contract: Before the change, prompt only accepted a bool show_default and the Option code deliberately forwarded only bool values; the commit adds a versionchanged 8.3.3 note for the new string form.

C.label: bug
C.description: A string show_default was ignored in the prompt text.
C.contract: Documented show_default string should be displayed in prompts.

T.label: feature
T.description: Adds custom default labels to prompts through string-valued show_default.
T.contract: The previous prompt signature accepted only bool, its comment explicitly excluded non-boolean forwarding, and the new versionchanged entry announces string support.

B.label: bug
B.description: The Windows temp-file pager opened its file in binary mode ('wb'), so writing text through echo_via_pager/get_pager_file raised 'a bytes-like object is required' and color handling was skipped.
B.contract: echo_via_pager and get_pager_file accept text on every platform (issues 3731, 3740); the tests check text and ANSI handling on that backend.

C.label: bug
C.description: Tempfile pager opened the file in binary mode and failed on text writes.
C.contract: Pager accepts text

B.label: bug
B.description: The ANSI-stripping regex only matched CSI sequences made of digits, ';' and '?' followed by a letter, so valid sequences such as colon-delimited true-color SGR, mouse reports, intermediate-byte or '~'-terminated codes were left in unstyle()/strip_ansi output and miscounted by term_len.
B.contract: unstyle()/strip_ansi are meant to remove ANSI escape sequences (an existing test_unstyle_other_ansi already covers non-SGR codes); valid ECMA-48 CSI sequences surviving is a wrong result.

C.label: bug
C.description: strip_ansi regex only matched simple SGR sequences and left other CSI sequences (colon-delimited, intermediates) in output.
C.contract: strip_ansi should remove ANSI sequences

B.label: bug
B.description: Option.get_default replaced default=True with flag_value for every flag, including boolean flags, so a negative flag declared with flag_value=False, default=True always resolved to False and prompted with the wrong default.
B.contract: A boolean flag with flag_value=False and default=True should be True when not passed (the long-standing negative-flag pattern, issue #3111); the commit's docstring describes the old result as silently always False.

C.label: bug
C.description: default=True on boolean flags was wrongly replaced by flag_value, producing False.
C.contract: For boolean flags True is a literal value.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: get_help_option_names now preserves the declaration order of help_option_names (via dict.fromkeys) instead of returning names in set order.
B.contract: The method never promised an order and the docstring adds '.. versionchanged:: 8.5.0 Names keep their declaration order'; the change targets reproducibility rather than a broken promise.

C.label: bug
C.description: Help option names came from a set so their order was nondeterministic.
C.contract: Help option order should be stable

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Help-option names acquire a deterministic declaration-order policy.
T.contract: The previous docstring promised option names but no ordering, while the new versionchanged entry explicitly introduces declaration-order preservation.

B.label: bug
B.description: CliRunner's _NamedTextIOWrapper inherited TextIOWrapper's close/finalizer behaviour and closed the BytesIO buffers owned by StreamMixer, so later writes or reads (e.g. from logging handlers) hit 'I/O operation on closed file'.
B.contract: The wrapped buffers belong to StreamMixer and must stay usable after a wrapper is closed or collected; issues #824 and #3110 report ValueError on closed file with logging in CliRunner as a regression.

C.label: bug
C.description: CliRunner wrapper closed the shared buffers on garbage collection, causing closed-file errors.
C.contract: Wrappers must not close buffers owned elsewhere (issues 824, 2993, 3110).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Options whose flag_value is a non-basic object (class, enum, frozenset) default to UNPROCESSED and pass the object through, where the guessed STRING type stringified it.
B.contract: Existing tests explicitly documented that exotic flag values are rendered to strings unless type=UNPROCESSED is given, and the commit adds a versionchanged 8.4 note describing the new default.

C.label: bug
C.description: Non-basic flag_value (e.g. Enum, class) was stringified because type was not auto-detected as UNPROCESSED.
C.contract: Flag values should be passed through unchanged (issue 3363).

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Automatic flag-value type selection passes non-basic Python objects through unchanged rather than converting them to strings.
T.contract: Existing tests explicitly expected stringification, and the version-change documentation identifies explicit UNPROCESSED as the established way to preserve such objects.

B.label: bug
B.description: Context.lookup_default returned the internal UNSET sentinel instead of None for missing keys, which leaked the sentinel through the public API and broke subclass overrides that fall back when the parent returns None.
B.contract: lookup_default is public and returned None for a missing key; issue #3145 reports overridden lookup_default fallbacks no longer being honoured.

C.label: bug
C.description: lookup_default returned the internal UNSET sentinel and overrides were ignored.
C.contract: Public lookup_default should return None for missing keys and be respected by overrides.

B.label: bug
B.description: FishComplete emitted each completion as newline-separated type/value/help lines, which fish's command substitution splits into separate entries, so the fish completion script could not parse them and completion broke.
B.contract: Fish completion worked with the 'type,value<TAB>help' format before the 8.4.0 change (#3126); the commit message names it a regression, and the fish complete docs require one argument per line with an optional tab-separated description.

C.label: bug
C.description: Fish completion script and output format broke completion for plain items after a regression.
C.contract: Completion must work in fish; regression from 8.4.0 stated in message.

B.label: feature
B.description: A string value in default_map for a multi-value (nargs > 1 or tuple-typed) parameter is split with the type's split_envvar_value, so default_map can supply such values as a single string.
B.contract: default_map values were type-cast as given and a plain string was never accepted for multi-value parameters; splitting them like environment variables is a newly supported input form.

C.label: bug
C.description: A string in default_map for a multi-value parameter was not split, causing a usage error.
C.contract: default_map should behave like envvar for nargs parameters.

T.label: feature
T.description: Adds support for whitespace-separated strings in default_map for multi-value parameters by splitting them before conversion.
T.contract: The added tests call this a regression, but the packet establishes no prior promise that default_map accepts unstructured strings for multi-value parameters; environment-variable splitting alone does not establish that contract.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: With hide_input=True, prompt shows the validation error message with the entered value masked, replacing the fixed generic 'The value you entered was invalid.' message.
B.contract: The old code deliberately replaced the message for hidden input to avoid leaking the value; showing a masked custom message is an enhancement of the error output, not a repair of a broken promise.

C.label: bug
C.description: Custom error messages from converters were hidden in prompts with hide_input=True.
C.contract: Custom validation messages should be shown, with the secret value masked (issue 3256).

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Hidden-input validation displays detailed, masked error messages rather than a generic invalid-value message.
T.contract: The existing implementation deliberately emitted an accurate generic error to hide input; the packet supplies no prior promise of detailed messages in this mode.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Deprecates CliRunner.isolated_filesystem with a DeprecationWarning and migrates the test suite to tmp_path.
B.contract: A deprecation ('.. deprecated:: 8.5.0'); the F2P test fails only because no warning was emitted before.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Deprecates CliRunner.isolated_filesystem.
C.contract: Deprecation

B.label: bug
B.description: When an error was raised while paging, _tempfilepager skipped closing the temp file before os.unlink, so on Windows a PermissionError replaced the original exception.
B.contract: Errors raised inside the pager must propagate unchanged; the commit fixes issue 3731 and the test checks the file is closed before unlink.

C.label: bug
C.description: Temp file not closed before unlink in pager error path, masking the original exception on Windows.
C.contract: Original exception must propagate

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: FuncParamType reports the ValueError's own message in BadParameter, falling back to the raw value only when the message is empty, where it always used the raw value as the message.
B.contract: The old code deliberately stringified the value as the failure message; the change enriches the error text rather than correcting a wrong or missing message.

C.label: bug
C.description: FuncParamType failed with the input value instead of the ValueError message.
C.contract: User-raised ValueError message should be reported.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Function parameter conversion errors include the underlying ValueError explanation when available.
