B.label: bug
B.description: The URL regex's tail only allowed '/' or '?' after the authority, rejecting valid absolute URLs such as http://example.org#fragment.
B.contract: RFC 3986 permits a fragment after an empty path; validate.URL promises to accept valid URLs and already accepted '/foo?bar#baz'.

C.label: bug
C.description: URL validator regex rejected a fragment directly after empty path.
C.contract: RFC 3986 allows fragment after empty path

B.label: bug
B.description: Schema._deserialize always passed its partial value (default False) to nested fields, overriding a nested schema instance's own partial setting, so Nested(SchemaA(partial=('x',))) still required 'x'.
B.contract: A schema instance's partial argument should govern its loads, including when nested, unless the parent load explicitly passes partial; the parent here passed nothing.

C.label: bug
C.description: Default partial=False on nested schema overrode parent partial, causing wrong required errors.
C.contract: Nested schema should inherit partial from parent when unspecified (issue 2149).

B.label: bug
B.description: Per-item post_load processors with pass_original zipped processed data with the original data using zip, silently dropping items that a collection-level processor had appended.
B.contract: Regression test for issue #1755: load must return everything the processors produce; a pass_original processor must not truncate the collection.

C.label: bug
C.description: post_load with pass_original used zip, dropping items appended by processors.
C.contract: All items must reach processors

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends validate.URL hostname patterns to accept internationalized (Unicode) domain names.
B.contract: The hostname regex was ASCII-only by design; the commit explicitly adds IDN support as a new supported input.

C.label: feature
C.description: validate.URL gains support for internationalized domain names.
C.contract: New supported input

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Moves the check for fields declared as classes from schema instantiation to class declaration time.
B.contract: The same TypeError existed before at instantiation; the commit deliberately raises it earlier and updates the test accordingly.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Moves the check for fields declared as classes to class declaration time.
C.contract: Earlier error reporting

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes allow_none default to True for by_value Enum fields whose enum contains a None-valued member.
B.contract: allow_none previously followed the generic Field default (False); the commit 'improves the default' and documents the new default in the docstring.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Enum by_value fields default allow_none True when an enum member has None value.
C.contract: Default change

B.label: bug
B.description: Email validation fell back to IDNA-encoding the domain and the punycode form passed the ASCII regex even when a Unicode label started or ended with a hyphen, so invalid domains like user@-münchen.de were accepted.
B.contract: The Email domain regex forbids hyphens at label boundaries and rejects the ASCII equivalents; the validator should reject invalid domains regardless of script.

C.label: bug
C.description: Email validator domain regex did not properly handle IDNs and hyphen boundaries.
C.contract: Valid IDN emails should be accepted

B.label: bug
B.description: validate.URL required a hostname for every scheme, so standard host-less file URLs such as file:///tmp/x were rejected even when 'file' was an allowed scheme.
B.contract: file:///path is the canonical file URL form (empty host means localhost); the validator accepted the equivalent file://localhost/path, so allowing the file scheme implies accepting it.

C.label: bug
C.description: URL validator rejected valid file:/// URLs without a hostname.
C.contract: file URLs may omit hostname

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Turns Number and Mapping into abstract base classes so instantiating them raises TypeError.
B.contract: They were documented as base classes not to use in schemas but were instantiable; this is a deliberate API tightening.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Number and Mapping made abstract base classes.
C.contract: Design change

B.label: bug
B.description: MarkdownRenderer always delimited code spans with a single backtick, so code containing backticks closed the span early on re-parse.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer output must re-parse to the same document; CommonMark requires the delimiter run to be longer than any backtick run inside.

C.label: bug
C.description: Code span rendering used a single backtick delimiter even when content contained backticks.
C.contract: Round-trip must preserve code spans.

B.label: bug
B.description: The include directive parsed included Markdown files without normalising CRLF line endings, so directive arguments kept a trailing '\r' and nested includes looked up wrong file names.
B.contract: Top-level input has its line endings normalised; included files must be handled the same way, so circular includes are detected rather than reported as missing files.

C.label: bug
C.description: Included markdown files with CRLF line endings were not normalized so include parsing failed (circular include not detected).
C.contract: Include directive should handle files with CRLF.

B.label: bug
B.description: Footnote bodies were parsed in a fresh BlockState instead of a child state, so link reference definitions inside a footnote were not registered and rendered as literal text.
B.contract: Link reference definitions are valid inside container blocks and must be consumed and resolved; the footnote rendering produced literal '[ref]: /url' text.

C.label: bug
C.description: Footnote body was parsed with a fresh BlockState so reference definitions inside footnotes were lost instead of shared with the document state.
C.contract: Reference definitions in a footnote body are expected to resolve links.

B.label: bug
B.description: MarkdownRenderer emitted escaped '*'/'_' text tokens unescaped, so literal markers such as \*not emphasis\* became emphasis after a re-parse.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer output must re-parse to the same document (round-trip tests); escaped backticks were already re-escaped.

C.label: bug
C.description: Escaped literal emphasis markers were re-emitted unescaped, turning text into emphasis.
C.contract: Markdown renderer round-trip must preserve literal text.

B.label: bug
B.description: parse_link_href treated a backslash before any character as an escape, so '\ ' swallowed the space into the destination and produced an invalid href.
B.contract: CommonMark only treats a backslash as an escape before ASCII punctuation; [a](foo\ bar) is not a link.

C.label: bug
C.description: Backslash was treated as an escape before any character, including non-punctuation, producing illegal href.
C.contract: CommonMark: backslash escapes only ASCII punctuation.

B.label: bug
B.description: parse_inline_footnote checked membership in the footnotes list instead of the footnote_indexes dict it maintains, making parsing quadratic in the number of footnote references.
B.contract: The index mapping already existed for constant-time lookups; the quadratic behaviour is reported as a denial-of-service defect, and the test checks that membership uses the mapping.

C.label: bug
C.description: Inline footnote parsing used O(n) list membership instead of the existing index dict, giving quadratic behaviour.
C.contract: The footnote_indexes mapping exists for constant-time lookup; quadratic DoS is a defect.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes MarkdownRenderer reproduce blank lines at the start of a document instead of dropping them.
B.contract: Leading blank lines carry no Markdown meaning and the renderer normalises blank lines elsewhere; preserving them is a new formatting policy rather than a broken promise.

C.label: bug
C.description: MarkdownRenderer dropped leading blank lines from the document.
C.contract: Round trip preserves content

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The renderer changes its formatting policy to preserve the number of leading blank lines.
T.contract: The round-trip test context suggests preservation intent, but the packet establishes no prior promise to preserve semantically insignificant leading whitespace.

B.label: bug
B.description: block_quote stripped trailing '>', spaces and newlines from the rendered quote with rstrip('> \n'), also eating a '>' that ended the content such as an autolink or HTML tag.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer output must preserve content on a round trip; '> <https://example.com>' must stay an autolink.

C.label: bug
C.description: Block quote rendering stripped trailing '>' characters from content such as autolinks.
C.contract: Round-trip must preserve content.

B.label: bug
B.description: markdown() decided a renderer was a built-in selector with renderer == 'html', so a renderer object whose __eq__ matches 'html' was sent to the lru_cache and crashed as unhashable.
B.contract: Renderer instances must be used as given; only the strings 'html'/'ast' select built-in cached parsers.

C.label: bug
C.description: markdown() compared renderer with == against builtin names, so an object with custom __eq__ was treated as builtin and hashing failed.
C.contract: Custom renderer instances must be honored by markdown().

B.label: bug
B.description: The def_list plugin regexes required the ':' marker at column 0, so definition markers indented by 1-3 spaces were not recognised.
B.contract: The plugin follows PHP Markdown Extra definition lists, which, like other Markdown block markers, allow up to three spaces of indentation before the colon.

C.label: bug
C.description: Definition-list marker regexes only matched ':' at column 0, so markers indented 1-3 spaces were not recognised.
C.contract: PHP Markdown Extra / CommonMark allow 0-3 spaces indentation of block markers.

B.label: bug
B.description: When recompiling list break rules for a shallow list item, the code replaced the first '3' in each rule pattern, corrupting the fenced directive's '{3,}' marker quantifier so a single ':' started a directive inside lists.
B.contract: A fenced directive needs at least three markers both inside and outside lists; the recompilation was only meant to relax the leading indent bound.

C.label: bug
C.description: List break rule recompilation replaced the first "3" in any pattern, corrupting fenced directive quantifier {3,}.
C.contract: Directive fence needs three or more markers inside lists too.

B.label: bug
B.description: create_markdown ignored an explicit escape argument when given an HTMLRenderer instance, so escape=False still escaped raw HTML.
B.contract: The docstring says escape applies when using the HTML renderer; a custom HTMLRenderer subclass silently ignored the flag.

C.label: bug
C.description: create_markdown ignored the escape argument when a custom HTMLRenderer instance was given.
C.contract: escape parameter documented as controlling HTML escaping.

B.label: bug
B.description: After an unterminated <...> link destination, _parse_link_href returned len(src) as the resume position, so later valid links in the same text were never parsed.
B.contract: A failed link attempt must leave the rest of the text to be parsed normally; '[bar](/url)' after a failed '[](<foo' must still render as a link.

C.label: bug
C.description: A failed angle-bracket link destination returned end-of-source as the scan position, hiding later valid links.
C.contract: Failed link parse should not swallow subsequent valid links.

B.label: bug
B.description: markdown() cached parsers in a dict keyed by (escape, renderer, plugins), so a list of plugins raised TypeError (unhashable) and a shared custom renderer reused a cached parser with stale escape state.
B.contract: plugins is documented as an iterable and calls such as markdown(text, plugins=['table']) are valid; each call must honour its escape argument.

C.label: bug
C.description: markdown() cache keyed on unhashable plugin lists and cached custom renderers/consumed iterables, raising TypeError or returning stale results.
C.contract: markdown() should accept plugin iterables and custom renderers correctly.

B.label: bug
B.description: The inline HTML comment regex implemented the old comment rules, rejecting comments such as <!-->, <!---> and comments containing '--' that CommonMark 0.31.2 recognises.
B.contract: mistune documents compatibility with CommonMark 0.31.2, and the spec examples in the commonmark.json fixtures (raw_html 625/626) expect these to be comments.

C.label: bug
C.description: Inline HTML comment regex did not follow CommonMark 0.31.2 rules.
C.contract: CommonMark spec conformance

B.label: bug
B.description: _parse_angle_link_href rejected any backslash inside a <...> link destination instead of treating it as an escape, so [link](<foo\*bar>) was not parsed as a link.
B.contract: CommonMark allows backslash escapes inside pointy-bracket link destinations.

C.label: bug
C.description: Angle-bracket link destinations rejected any backslash instead of treating it as an escape.
C.contract: CommonMark permits backslash escapes inside <...> destinations.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds MarkdownRenderer methods for strikethrough, mark and insert tokens.
B.contract: The MarkdownRenderer never supported these plugin tokens; the commit adds rendering support for them.

C.label: feature
C.description: MarkdownRenderer renders strikethrough, mark and insert tokens.
C.contract: New renderer support

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Changes default TOC heading id generation to skip ids already present in raw HTML of the document.
B.contract: The default heading_id produced deterministic toc_N ids by design; deduplicating against ids in user-supplied HTML is a new hardening policy.

C.label: bug
C.description: Auto-generated TOC heading ids could collide with ids already in the HTML source.
C.contract: Generated heading ids should be unique.

T.label: bug
T.description: Automatic heading ID generation ignored existing HTML IDs, creating duplicate anchors that could direct TOC links to the wrong element.
T.contract: Generated TOC links must identify their corresponding headings uniquely, including when supported raw HTML contains IDs.

B.label: bug
B.description: MarkdownRenderer wrote an empty reference destination as '[r]: ' instead of '[r]: <>', producing text that no longer parses as a reference definition.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer must emit Markdown equivalent to its input (round-trip tests); an empty destination must be written as <>.

C.label: bug
C.description: MarkdownRenderer emitted an empty reference destination as nothing, producing invalid non-round-tripping markdown.
C.contract: Renderer round trip must preserve content; empty destination needs explicit <>.

B.label: bug
B.description: Nested image syntax was parsed recursively without any depth limit, so deeply nested images raised RecursionError.
B.contract: Rendering Markdown input must not crash; the parser already caps emphasis depth and the security tests require bounded handling of nested input.

C.label: bug
C.description: Deeply nested image input recursed without bound causing RecursionError; no image depth limit.
C.contract: Parser should not crash on deep input (existing emphasis depth limit analog).

B.label: bug
B.description: MarkdownRenderer always emitted headings in ATX form, so a multi-line setext heading lost its continuation lines (they became a paragraph) when the output was re-parsed.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer output must re-parse to the same document (round-trip test suite); a multi-line heading must remain one heading.

C.label: bug
C.description: MarkdownRenderer emitted multi-line setext headings as ATX, breaking round-trip.
C.contract: Renderer output must re-parse to the same document.

B.label: bug
B.description: The Figure directive copied the figwidth option into the style attribute without validating it, allowing CSS injection such as '10px;position:fixed'.
B.contract: The image directives validate width/height against a numeric pattern before emitting styles (the Image directive already rejected such injection).

C.label: bug
C.description: Figure directive copied figwidth option unvalidated into style, allowing CSS injection.
C.contract: Image directive already validates dimensions; figure width should be validated equally.

B.label: bug
B.description: MarkdownRenderer wrapped link and image titles in double quotes without escaping embedded quotes or backslashes, so the re-parsed title ended early and the link broke.
B.contract: MarkdownRenderer output must re-parse to the same document (round-trip tests).

C.label: bug
C.description: Quotes and backslashes in link/image titles were not escaped when rendering markdown.
C.contract: Round-trip must preserve titles.

B.label: bug
B.description: The ordered-list bullet regex used \d{0,9}, so a bare '.' or ')' without digits was accepted as an ordered list marker.
B.contract: CommonMark (which mistune claims compatibility with) defines an ordered list marker as 1-9 digits followed by '.' or ')'.

C.label: bug
C.description: Ordered list marker regex allowed zero digits so a bare "." matched as a marker.
C.contract: Ordered markers require at least one digit (CommonMark)

B.label: bug
B.description: Failed link candidates over deeply nested brackets were re-scanned for every opening bracket, giving super-linear parse time on bracket-heavy input.
B.contract: The project's security tests require nested bracket input to be handled within a fixed deadline; the fix adds a high-water mark so failed spans are not rescanned.

C.label: bug
C.description: Failed bracket link candidates were re-scanned repeatedly (quadratic) and nested-link detection returned early incorrectly.
C.contract: Parser must handle nested bracket input in bounded time and keep nested links.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Adds explicit validation to chunked_even: n=0 now yields nothing and negative n raises ValueError('n must be at least 0').
B.contract: Invalid sizes already raised ValueError (from islice); the commit picks a new result for n=0 and a clearer error message for negative n.

C.label: bug
C.description: chunked_even did not handle n==0 or negative n, misbehaving instead of matching chunked.
C.contract: chunked/ichunked semantics: n=0 yields nothing, negative raises ValueError.

T.label: feature
T.description: The change adds support for zero-sized chunks yielding nothing and improves the exception message for negative sizes.
T.contract: The packet shows zero becoming accepted input but supplies no pre-existing promise that zero must work; negative sizes already raised ValueError.

B.label: bug
B.description: numeric_range.__reversed__ fetched the last element unconditionally, so reversing an empty range raised IndexError.
B.contract: numeric_range is a Sequence; reversed() of an empty sequence must yield nothing (issue #1152).

C.label: bug
C.description: reversed(numeric_range) on an empty range raised IndexError.
C.contract: reversed of an empty sequence should be empty.

B.label: feature
B.description: Lets the running_* functions accept maxlen objects implementing __index__ by converting them with operator.index.
B.contract: maxlen was handled as a plain int; accepting index-protocol objects is a newly supported input type (non-integers were already rejected).

C.label: bug
C.description: running_* functions did not coerce window size via __index__ so index-protocol integers raised TypeError.
C.contract: Integer-like window sizes should be accepted; floats rejected.

T.label: bug
T.description: Running-window functions compared size objects directly with integers before converting them through the index protocol, rejecting valid integer-like sizes.
T.contract: An integer window-size parameter should honor Python's index protocol; the failing test demonstrates equivalence to the already-supported integer size of two.

B.label: bug
B.description: ichunked with n=0 on a non-empty iterable consumed the first item and then crashed with an islice ValueError instead of yielding nothing like chunked.
B.contract: ichunked is documented as being like chunked, which yields nothing for n=0; the existing test_zero already expected an empty result for n=0.

C.label: bug
C.description: ichunked with n=0 or negative n did not match chunked (consumed/produced wrongly).
C.contract: ichunked documented as the lazy equivalent of chunked.

B.label: bug
B.description: exactly_n passed n+1 to islice, which raised ValueError for n <= -2 instead of returning False.
B.contract: The existing test already expected exactly_n([True], -1) to be False, so negative n is supported input.

C.label: bug
C.description: exactly_n failed for negative n (islice ValueError) and was inefficient for large n.
C.contract: exactly_n should return False for negative n, not raise.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds seekable.__getitem__ to index into the internal cache.
B.contract: seekable was not subscriptable; the commit adds and documents the new API.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds seekable.__getitem__ to read cached items.
C.contract: New capability.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds __class_getitem__ to peekable so peekable[T] works at runtime.
B.contract: peekable never supported subscripting; the commit adds generic alias support.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds __class_getitem__ to peekable for generic subscripting.
C.contract: New capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: numeric_range slicing computed bounds without accounting for negative steps, so e.g. numeric_range(10, 0, -2)[::-1] returned an empty range.
B.contract: numeric_range slicing must follow Python sequence slice semantics like range.

C.label: bug
C.description: numeric_range slicing with a negative step returned a wrong (empty/incorrect) range.
C.contract: Slicing should match range semantics.

B.label: bug
B.description: bucket's defaultdict cache created an empty entry on every membership test or lookup, so iterating the bucket reported keys that never appeared in the input.
B.contract: Iterating a bucket must yield only keys seen in the iterable (issue #1284).

C.label: bug
C.description: bucket used a defaultdict so lookups/membership tests invented phantom keys.
C.contract: Failed lookups must not add keys to the bucket.

B.label: bug
B.description: polynomial_from_roots reduced over nested lazy convolve generators, raising RecursionError for large numbers of roots.
B.contract: The function must handle any valid list of roots; 1500 roots is valid input.

C.label: bug
C.description: polynomial_from_roots used recursive reduce nesting that hit RecursionError for many roots.
C.contract: Should work for large inputs.

B.label: bug
B.description: product_index called len() on the raw element and args instead of the materialised tuples, raising TypeError for iterator input.
B.contract: product_index accepts iterables; the arguments were already converted to tuples for this reason.

C.label: bug
C.description: product_index took len() of the original element rather than the materialized tuple, failing for iterator input.
C.contract: Function already materialized inputs; iterators should work.

B.label: bug
B.description: peekable slicing with a negative step and omitted stop normalised stop to a negative value and cached the entire source, over-reading (or never finishing on an infinite iterator) for slices like p[5::-1].
B.contract: peekable documents full caching only for negative indices; p[5::-1] needs only the first six items.

C.label: bug
C.description: peekable negative-step slice with omitted stop cached the whole iterable instead of just up to start.
C.contract: Slicing should only consume what is needed.

B.label: bug
B.description: last() checked hasattr(iterable, '__reversed__'), so an object with __reversed__ = None was treated as reversible and reported as empty.
B.contract: Per the Python data model, __reversed__ = None marks an object as not reversible; last() should fall back to iteration (issue #1001).

C.label: bug
C.description: last() used hasattr for __reversed__ so a class setting it to None raised instead of falling back to iteration.
C.contract: Python protocol: __reversed__ = None means unsupported; last must still work.

B.label: bug
B.description: seekable(maxlen=0).peek() pushed the peeked item back by wrapping the source in a new chain on every call, so repeated peeks or truth tests grew memory without bound.
B.contract: Peeking must not leak memory; a one-item lookahead needs constant space.

C.label: bug
C.description: seekable.peek with maxlen=0 re-chained the source on every call, growing memory without bound.
C.contract: Repeated peek must use bounded memory.

B.label: bug
B.description: bucket used `validator or default`, so a falsy callable validator was silently replaced by the accept-all default.
B.contract: Any callable passed as validator must be applied (issue #1308).

C.label: bug
C.description: bucket replaced a falsey validator with the default because it used truthiness instead of an is-None check.
C.contract: A supplied validator callable must be honoured.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes chunked raise ValueError('n must be at least 0') for negative n up front.
B.contract: Negative n already raised ValueError from islice; only the error message changes.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: chunked with negative n now raises a clear ValueError message up front.
C.contract: Previously already raised a ValueError (from islice); only message/early check changed.

B.label: bug
B.description: iequals padded shorter iterables with a sentinel fill value, so an element that compares equal to anything (e.g. mock.ANY) made iterables of different lengths compare equal.
B.contract: iequals must return False for iterables of different lengths (issue #900).

C.label: bug
C.description: iequals used an object() fillvalue compared with all_equal so an item equal to anything (mock.ANY) faked equality.
C.contract: iequals must return False for different lengths.

B.label: bug
B.description: one() and only() used `too_long or ValueError(msg)`, dropping falsy user exceptions and eagerly building the default message, which called repr on items even when a custom exception was supplied.
B.contract: When too_short/too_long are given, that exception must be raised.

C.label: bug
C.description: one()/only() used truthiness so a falsy user-supplied exception was ignored.
C.contract: Supplied too_short/too_long exceptions must be raised.

B.label: bug
B.description: interleave_evenly crashed with IndexError when given no iterables instead of yielding nothing.
B.contract: An empty collection of iterables is valid input and interleaving zero iterables yields an empty result.

C.label: bug
C.description: interleave_evenly with no iterables raised IndexError.
C.contract: Empty input should yield an empty iterator.

B.label: bug
B.description: With maxlen=0, seekable.peek() and bool() consumed an item that the zero-length cache could not hold, silently dropping it from later iteration.
B.contract: peek and truth testing must not consume items (issue #1268).

C.label: bug
C.description: seekable.peek/bool dropped an item when maxlen=0 because the consumed item could not be cached.
C.contract: peek must not consume items.

B.label: bug
B.description: gray_product and partial_product repeated the argument tuple before materialising it, so with repeat>1 the same iterator object was shared and exhausted, giving wrong output or a spurious ValueError.
B.contract: Results with iterator arguments must equal those with the equivalent sequences, as repeat=n is documented as repeating the iterables.

C.label: bug
C.description: gray_product/partial_product multiplied the raw iterables tuple before materializing, so iterator arguments with repeat were exhausted by the first copy.
C.contract: repeat with iterator arguments should equal repeat with sequences.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Adds a ValueError for negative n in sliced.
B.contract: Negative slice sizes are invalid input with no documented behaviour; the commit adds argument validation where garbage was returned before.

C.label: bug
C.description: sliced with negative n silently returned a wrong result instead of raising.
C.contract: Negative slice size is invalid input and should raise.

T.label: bug
T.description: Missing negative-size validation allowed sliced() to yield misleading slices for an impossible chunk size.
T.contract: A chunk size represents a nonnegative item count; the test explicitly identifies silent incorrect output for negative sizes.

B.label: bug
B.description: value_chain wrapped `yield from value` in try/except TypeError, so a TypeError raised while consuming an iterable was swallowed and the iterable object itself was yielded as a scalar.
B.contract: Only non-iterable arguments are emitted as-is; errors raised during iteration must propagate (issue #1250).

C.label: bug
C.description: value_chain wrapped the whole iteration in try/except TypeError so TypeErrors raised while iterating were swallowed and the object yielded as a scalar.
C.contract: Only non-iterable arguments should be yielded as-is; errors inside iteration must propagate.

B.label: bug
B.description: The windowed running_min/running_max used non-strict comparisons when pruning the monotonic deque, so among equal values the newest won instead of the earliest as builtin min/max return.
B.contract: Windowed results are expected to equal min()/max() over each window, and the unwindowed path (accumulate with min/max) is already stable.

C.label: bug
C.description: Windowed running_min/max popped equal values, giving unstable results where ties returned the newer element instead of the older like min()/max().
C.contract: running_min/max should match builtin min/max tie semantics.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Adds a ValueError for negative n in tail, including the sized-iterable path that returned an empty result.
B.contract: Negative n is invalid input; rejecting it is new argument validation (the iterator path only failed incidentally inside deque).

C.label: bug
C.description: tail with negative n returned wrong/odd results instead of raising ValueError.
C.contract: Negative size is invalid input.

T.label: bug
T.description: tail() failed to reject negative sizes on its sized-input path, producing behavior inconsistent with equivalent iterator input.
T.contract: The iterator negative-size test already passes before the change, establishing rejection that must also hold for sized inputs.

B.label: bug
B.description: License-File validation only rejected absolute paths, so Windows drive-relative paths such as 'C:LICENSE' passed although they escape the project root.
B.contract: License-File paths must be relative to the project root; the validator already rejects absolute paths and '..' for this reason.

C.label: bug
C.description: License-file validation accepted Windows drive-relative paths like C:LICENSE.
C.contract: Metadata spec requires relative paths that do not escape root.

B.label: bug
B.description: _build_tag_regex was not anchored at the end, so a build tag containing a newline matched up to the newline and parse_wheel_filename silently accepted a truncated build tag.
B.contract: parse_wheel_filename must raise InvalidWheelFilename for malformed build tags; the name component already used a \Z anchor for the same reason (#1341).

C.label: bug
C.description: Wheel build tag regex was unanchored so a build part with a newline suffix was accepted with the suffix cut.
C.contract: PEP 427 build tag must be digits followed by valid text; invalid filenames must be rejected.

B.label: bug
B.description: The tokenizer's END rule used '$', which also matches before a trailing newline, so requirements and markers with a trailing '\n' were accepted.
B.contract: Parsing must consume the whole input; trailing line breaks are invalid, as the new tests and the '\r' cases show.

C.label: bug
C.description: Tokenizer END rule used "$" which matches before a trailing newline, accepting inputs ending with a line break.
C.contract: Parser must require the true end of input.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes Metadata.from_email report unparsed-field errors and from_raw validation errors together in one ExceptionGroup.
B.contract: The previous test explicitly expected a single exception for unparsed input; the commit deliberately extends error aggregation.

C.label: bug
C.description: Metadata.from_email stopped at unparsed-field errors and did not report other validation errors such as missing required fields.
C.contract: validate=True is meant to aggregate all errors.

T.label: bug
T.description: Encountering unparsed email fields raised an exception group before raw metadata validation could contribute its independent errors.
T.contract: The existing grouped-validation machinery and 'invalid or unparsed metadata' wrapper support collecting validation failures; the failing tests expose missing structured errors, not merely changed wording.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes Pylock.select raise PylockSelectError for extras or dependency groups not declared in the lock file.
B.contract: Labelled feat and documented as versionchanged 26.4; unknown extras and groups were silently accepted before.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Pylock.select now raises PylockSelectError for undeclared extras and dependency groups, previously silently ignored.
C.contract: Deliberate validation policy added (versionchanged note).

B.label: bug
B.description: The tokenizer's URL rule [^ \t]+ also matched line breaks, so a URL could absorb a newline and following text that later serialises as an extra requirement line.
B.contract: Requirements reject trailing and embedded line breaks (existing test_error_when_suffixed_with_line_break for version and marker forms); a URL is a single whitespace-free token.

C.label: bug
C.description: URL token regex allowed embedded line breaks, enabling injection of a second requirement line.
C.contract: Requirement must be a single line; line breaks must be rejected.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Adds validation that interpreter tag components are identifiers, so tags like '2.7.6-none-any' raise InvalidTag.
B.contract: The documented InvalidTag conditions only covered empty components and wrong component counts; the commit tightens validation and rewrites the docs.

C.label: bug
C.description: parse_tag accepted non-identifier interpreter components such as 2.7.6, expanding malformed wheel names into bogus tags.
C.contract: Interpreter tag must be a valid identifier.

T.label: bug
T.description: Tag parsing omitted interpreter validation, allowing malformed wheel tags to expand into numeric or otherwise invalid interpreter identifiers.
T.contract: Parsing wheel compatibility tags must reject malformed interpreter components rather than produce apparently valid tags from filenames such as the supplied 2.7.6 example.

B.label: bug
B.description: The arbitrary-equality branch of the specifier regex used '*' so '===' with no version was accepted in specifiers and requirements.
B.contract: The PEP 440/508 grammar requires a non-empty version after a comparison operator; '==' without a version was already rejected.

C.label: bug
C.description: Specifier regex allowed an empty arbitrary-equality version ("===").
C.contract: An empty arbitrary version is invalid.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Changes canonicalize_license_expression to unify case variants of a LicenseRef to the first spelling instead of the last.
B.contract: Case variants were already unified to one spelling; choosing the first occurrence is a new canonicalisation policy.

C.label: bug
C.description: canonicalize_license_expression mapped case variants of a LicenseRef to the last spelling, mangling identifiers instead of the first spelling.
C.contract: SPDX LicenseRef idstring is case-insensitive; canonical output should be consistent.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Canonicalization changes its representative spelling for case-equivalent LicenseRef identifiers from the last occurrence to the first.
T.contract: The supplied SPDX explanation makes case variants equivalent, and both implementations unify them; no existing first-occurrence spelling promise is shown.

B.label: bug
B.description: RFC822Policy only folded '\n' in header values, so a bare '\r' crashed writing with HeaderWriteError and other line boundaries could inject headers; Summary validation also only checked '\n'.
B.contract: Writing valid metadata must not crash and multi-line values must stay inside their header; Summary must be a single line.

C.label: bug
C.description: Metadata writer folded only "\n", so other line boundaries (e.g. bare \r) broke header writing or allowed header injection.
C.contract: Single-line fields must not contain line breaks; writing must be safe.

B.label: bug
B.description: cpython_tags, generic_tags and compatible_tags used `platforms or platform_tags()`, so an explicitly empty platforms list was replaced by the host platforms.
B.contract: Only None means 'use the current platform'; an explicit empty iterable must produce no platform-specific tags.

C.label: bug
C.description: Empty platforms iterable was treated as falsy and replaced by default platform tags.
C.contract: Explicit empty platforms should yield no tags.

B.label: bug
B.description: LowerBound/UpperBound with version None kept the inclusive flag, so two spellings of the same infinite bound each compared greater than the other.
B.contract: Bounds use total_ordering and must form a consistent order; an unbounded end is a single value.

C.label: bug
C.description: Unbounded LowerBound/UpperBound with different inclusive flags compared as distinct and sorted above each other.
C.contract: -inf/+inf should be single value for ordering and equality.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Caches the formatted string of Marker objects as a performance optimisation.
B.contract: Output was already correct; the tests only check string identity from caching.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Caches the formatted marker string for performance; tests check reuse of the cached string.
C.contract: Output equal, only a performance optimization.

B.label: bug
B.description: Value.serialize always wrapped marker values in double quotes, so a value containing '"' serialised into a different marker expression.
B.contract: str(Marker) and str(Requirement) must round-trip to an equivalent marker; the parser accepts single-quoted values containing double quotes.

C.label: bug
C.description: Marker value serialization always used double quotes so values containing a double quote produced a changed/invalid marker string.
C.contract: Round-trip serialization must preserve marker semantics.

B.label: bug
B.description: _url_name returned the last URL path segment without percent-decoding it, so a wheel URL containing %2B produced an invalid file name.
B.contract: A distribution's file name derived from its URL must be the actual file name; URL path components are percent-encoded.

C.label: bug
C.description: Pylock file name derived from a URL was not percent-decoded so local versions like +cu130 stayed encoded.
C.contract: Derived filename must be a valid wheel/sdist name.

B.label: bug
B.description: Pylock.select used `tags or sys_tags()`, so an explicitly empty tags sequence fell back to the host's tags and selected host-compatible wheels.
B.contract: Only None means 'use the running interpreter's tags'; an explicit empty sequence must match no wheels.

C.label: bug
C.description: Pylock.select used truthiness on tags so an explicitly empty tag list fell back to host tags.
C.contract: Explicit empty tags should be respected.

B.label: bug
B.description: _wheel_name_regex ended with '$', which matches before a trailing newline, so a wheel project name ending in '\n' was accepted.
B.contract: parse_wheel_filename must reject invalid project names with InvalidWheelFilename.

C.label: bug
C.description: Wheel name regex used "$" so a trailing newline in the project name was accepted.
C.contract: Invalid wheel filenames must be rejected.

B.label: bug
B.description: _parse_group treated any error already in the shared collector as a failure of the current group, so after a first parse error later sibling groups were never parsed and their errors went unreported.
B.contract: Dependency group resolution collects all errors at once (existing test_resolution_can_capture_multiple_errors_at_once).

C.label: bug
C.description: Dependency group resolver stopped collecting errors from sibling includes after the first parse error.
C.contract: Resolver is documented to collect multiple errors at once.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes Description-Content-Type accept the UTF-8 charset in any letter case.
B.contract: The previous test suite explicitly listed 'text/plain; charset=utf-8' as invalid, so exact-case matching was tested behaviour that is now relaxed.

C.label: bug
C.description: Charset check was case-sensitive so charset=utf-8 was rejected.
C.contract: Charset names are case-insensitive.

T.label: bug
T.description: A case-sensitive charset comparison rejected valid lowercase and mixed-case spellings of UTF-8.
T.contract: The validator promises to accept the UTF-8 charset, whose name is case-insensitive, so equivalent spellings must receive the same treatment.

B.label: bug
B.description: is_valid_pylock_path used re.match with a '$' anchor, which also matches before a trailing newline, so 'pylock.spam.toml\n' was accepted.
B.contract: PEP 751 lock file names must be exactly pylock.toml or pylock.<name>.toml.

C.label: bug
C.description: is_valid_pylock_path used regex match, so a trailing newline passed the "$" anchor.
C.contract: Pylock filename spec requires the whole name to match.

B.label: bug
B.description: Pylock.select tested `if self.environments`, so an explicitly empty environments list was treated as absent and no error was raised.
B.contract: The pylock spec quoted in the code says that when environments is specified an error must be raised if no expression is satisfied.

C.label: bug
C.description: Pylock.select used truthiness on environments so an explicitly empty list skipped the "no environment satisfied" error.
C.contract: Spec requires an error if no environment expression is satisfied.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Adds a fast path that skips ast.literal_eval for plain marker string literals.
B.contract: Results were already correct; the tests only check via mocking that literal_eval is not called (performance optimisation).

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Performance shortcut that skips ast.literal_eval for plain marker strings; output unchanged.
C.contract: Optimization only.

B.label: bug
B.description: The ~= specifier's pre/post/dev release groups were matched with IGNORECASE but not ASCII, so Unicode case-folding characters such as dotless i or long s were accepted.
B.contract: Specifiers must follow the ASCII PEP 440 grammar; the same defect was already fixed for local labels (issue #469).

C.label: bug
C.description: The ~= specifier regex groups lacked ASCII scoping so case-insensitive unicode characters matched pre/post-release words.
C.contract: Other operators already reject non-ASCII lookalikes (issue 469).

B.label: bug
B.description: _path_name split on '/' or '\\' exclusively, so paths mixing both separators kept a directory component and failed filename validation.
B.contract: pylock paths may use Windows separators and explicit POSIX separators; the filename must be the last component regardless of separator.

C.label: bug
C.description: _path_name handled only one kind of separator, wrong for paths with mixed Windows/POSIX separators.
C.contract: Filename of path with mixed separators must be the last component.

B.label: bug
B.description: Requirement let InvalidSpecifier from SpecifierSet escape instead of raising InvalidRequirement, also breaking __setstate__'s handling of invalid strings.
B.contract: Requirement documents that an invalid requirement string raises InvalidRequirement.

C.label: bug
C.description: Requirement raised InvalidSpecifier instead of InvalidRequirement for invalid specifier.
C.contract: Requirement constructor is documented to raise InvalidRequirement for bad input.

B.label: feature
B.description: extract_format accepts and ignores a sign specifier ('+', '-', ' ') in number formats, so patterns like '{:+.7f}' are parsed.
B.contract: The documented spec grammar was '[[fill]align][0][width][.precision][type]' with no sign component; the commit adds sign to the grammar and the test fails only because it was unsupported.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds support for sign specifiers in number formats.
C.contract: New format capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: Timezone offsets with minutes >= 60 were accepted and silently folded into the hour, so '+01:60' became +02:00.
B.contract: Out-of-range datetime components are rejected with ValueError (the datetime constructors do this for other fields); a parser should not silently produce a different offset.

C.label: bug
C.description: Timezone minutes of 60 or more were accepted silently.
C.contract: Timezone minutes must be in 0..59.

B.label: bug
B.description: The full-match regex was anchored with '^...$', and '$' also matches before a trailing newline, so parse('{}', 'test\n') succeeded while dropping the newline from the captured value.
B.contract: parse() must match the whole string exactly; the captured value should be 'test\n', not a silently truncated 'test'.

C.label: bug
C.description: Match regex used $ which allowed trailing newline to be dropped from the result.
C.contract: Full-string match must retain the trailing newline (issue 124).

B.label: bug
B.description: The f/F patterns always required a decimal point, so {:.0f} could not parse the output of format(x, '.0f').
B.contract: parse is documented as the opposite of format(); format(20.0, '.0f') yields '20' (issue #159).

C.label: bug
C.description: {:.0f} required a decimal point although zero-precision formatting emits none, so formatted values failed to parse.
C.contract: Parse should round-trip str.format output (issue 159).

B.label: bug
B.description: Year-less strftime formats were parsed with strptime's default year 1900 and the current year applied afterwards, so Feb 29 crashed and %j day numbers resolved in the wrong year.
B.contract: Year-less formats are documented and tested to use the current year (test_flexible_dates_year_current_year_inferred).

C.label: bug
C.description: Year-less strftime formats were parsed with strptime's default year 1900, so Feb 29 and day-of-year values resolved wrongly.
C.contract: Year-less formats are documented to use current year.

B.label: bug
B.description: strf_date_convert returned dt.time() for time-only formats, discarding the timezone parsed by %z.
B.contract: A parsed %z offset must be kept in the result, as it is for date-time results.

C.label: bug
C.description: Time-only strftime results dropped the timezone offset by returning dt.time().
C.contract: Parsed %z offset must be preserved.

B.label: bug
B.description: Month names were matched case-insensitively but looked up case-sensitively in MONTHS_MAP, so 'jul' or 'JUL' raised KeyError.
B.contract: Patterns are compiled with re.IGNORECASE by default, so any accepted spelling must convert.

C.label: bug
C.description: date_convert looked up month names case-sensitively though matching is case-insensitive, raising KeyError.
C.contract: Matching is case-insensitive by default so month names in any case must convert.

B.label: feature
B.description: Allows hyphens in field names by mapping them to valid regex group names.
B.contract: Field names were limited to \w characters; hyphenated names are newly supported (closes #86).

C.label: feature
C.description: Allows hyphen in field names.
C.contract: New accepted field-name syntax (closes issue 86).

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds support for ',' and '_' grouping characters in integer format specs.
B.contract: Grouping options were rejected as 'format spec not recognised'; the commit adds new format-spec support.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds grouping option (, and _) to the decimal format spec.
C.contract: New format capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: For '<' and '^' alignment the generated regex required at least one fill character after the value ('+'), so patterns like '{:^2S}' or 'Column {:d}:{:^}' failed to match text with no trailing padding.
B.contract: These patterns matched before the 1.17 change for #112 (issue #118 reports the regression); alignment fill is optional when the value fills or exceeds the width.

C.label: bug
C.description: Unused alignment generated a regex requiring at least one fill char, breaking matches.
C.contract: Regression introduced in 1.17 broke verbose formats (issue 118).

B.label: feature
B.description: Result.__getitem__ accepts slice objects and returns the corresponding slice of the fixed results.
B.contract: Only integer indexes and names were supported before; the commit (changelog 'Added slice access to fixed results') adds a new access form.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds slice access to Result.
C.contract: New capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: The %z regex contained capturing groups that the parser did not count, shifting the group index of every following field so later fields returned the wrong text.
B.contract: Each field must return its own matched text (issue #262).

C.label: bug
C.description: Group index was not advanced for capture groups generated by %z formats, shifting later fields.
C.contract: Later fields must read from correct groups.

B.label: bug
B.description: The numeric-type list used to add the sign prefix omitted 'F', so the Decimal type {:F} rejected signed numbers such as -12.1 (the commit also adds nan/inf).
B.contract: {:F} is the Decimal counterpart of {:f}, which accepts a sign (issue #249).

C.label: bug
C.description: The {:F} Decimal type did not accept a sign (and f/F did not accept nan/inf).
C.contract: {:f} accepts signs; {:F} should too.

B.label: bug
B.description: For fields not starting with a letter the parser took the format as field[1:], assuming a leading ':', so a numbered field with a type such as '{0:f}' yielded the spec ':f' and raised 'format spec not recognised'.
B.contract: Numbered fields like '{0}' were already accepted and format specs are supported on fields; '{0:f}' is valid format() syntax that crashed (issue #125).

C.label: bug
C.description: Numbered fields with types like {0:f} raised format spec not recognised.
C.contract: Digit field numbering with types should work (issue 125).

B.label: bug
B.description: The %z regex allowed a '|' sign (from the [+|-] class) and offsets without minutes, so such text matched and then crashed inside strptime with ValueError.
B.contract: A strftime-style field should only match text strptime can convert; non-matching input must yield no match rather than an exception.

C.label: bug
C.description: The %z regex accepted offsets strptime rejects (pipe sign, missing minutes, lowercase z), crashing in strptime.
C.contract: Pattern should match only what strptime accepts.

B.label: bug
B.description: The 'tt' type pattern made the time part optional, so it matched an empty string and produced a bogus time(0, 0).
B.contract: {:tt} is documented to parse a time; parse('{:tt}', '') must not match.

C.label: bug
C.description: The tt type pattern made the time itself optional, matching the empty string and producing a bogus time.
C.contract: Time type should require a time.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds support for the uppercase E, G and X format types.
B.contract: These types were explicitly rejected as 'not recognised'; the commit adds them as new supported specifiers.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds support for uppercase E, G and X format type specifiers.
C.contract: New accepted format types; tests fail because they were not recognised.

B.label: bug
B.description: Fractional seconds were converted with int(float('.' + u) * 1000000), losing precision through floating-point rounding (501902 became 501901).
B.contract: Parsed timestamps must keep the microseconds given in the input (issue #162).

C.label: bug
C.description: Fractional seconds were converted via float multiplication causing microsecond rounding errors.
C.contract: Microseconds parsed from a timestamp must be exact.

B.label: bug
B.description: AM/PM and Zulu markers were compared case-sensitively after case-insensitive matching, so '10:21:36 pm' converted to 10:21 and a lowercase 'z' offset was mishandled.
B.contract: Matching is case-insensitive by default, so accepted lowercase markers must convert correctly.

C.label: bug
C.description: Lowercase am/pm and lowercase z were not normalized before case-sensitive conversion.
C.contract: Matching is case-insensitive so conversion must be.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Changes slicing an Interval to return an Interval instead of a list of atomic intervals.
B.contract: The previous test explicitly asserted that slices return lists; the commit deliberately changes the return type.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Interval slicing now returns an Interval rather than a list of intervals.
C.contract: Deliberate API consistency change with test updates.

B.label: bug
B.description: from_string stopped at the first unparseable fragment and returned what it had parsed so far, silently ignoring invalid input such as '1' or '[0,1] | 1'.
B.contract: A parser must not silently drop input; issue #57 reports invalid strings being accepted, and the function now documents a ValueError for them.

C.label: bug
C.description: from_string silently ignored unparsable leftover text instead of raising ValueError.
C.contract: from_string is expected to raise ValueError on invalid strings (issue 57).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Changes IntervalDict.update (and construction) so the last provided value wins for overlapping intervals.
B.contract: The previous docstrings explicitly said there is no guarantee that the last value wins; the commit changes the documented contract.

C.label: bug
C.description: IntervalDict.update with overlapping intervals and mixed hashable/unhashable values or itself did not let the last value win.
C.contract: update should behave like dict.update, last value wins; self-update must be safe.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The commit establishes last-value-wins ordering for overlapping updates.
T.contract: The previous constructor and update documentation explicitly disclaimed this ordering guarantee; the failing tests enforce the newly introduced guarantee.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Changes IntervalDict.pop to treat an explicit None default as a real default value.
B.contract: The old docstring explicitly said a default is used only if it is not None, so the old behaviour was the documented one.

C.label: bug
C.description: IntervalDict.pop treated default=None as no default and raised KeyError.
C.contract: dict.pop semantics: explicit None default is returned.

T.label: feature
T.description: The commit adds support for None as an explicit fallback value in IntervalDict.pop.
T.contract: The previous documentation explicitly excluded None from usable defaults, and the failing assertion exercises that newly supported value.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes every ordering comparison involving an empty interval return False and deprecates comparing intervals with plain values.
B.contract: The previous tests explicitly asserted that empty intervals compare as both less and greater than other intervals (vacuous truth), so the old results were the tested semantics.

C.label: bug
C.description: Comparison operators on empty intervals returned True for some comparisons instead of False.
C.contract: Empty intervals should not compare as before/after anything.

T.label: bug
T.description: Interval comparisons omitted empty-operand checks, allowing an empty interval to compare strictly less than and greater than itself.
T.contract: Strict ordering should be irreflexive; the failing tests expose that invariant violation, although earlier tests explicitly accepted the defective results.

B.label: feature
B.description: Continues building the experimental AbstractDiscreteInterval: renames incr to step and adds normalisation of open bounds.
B.contract: The class is documented as experimental and incomplete; the tests come with a new test module for the new behaviour.

C.label: feature
C.description: Extends AbstractDiscreteInterval with a step attribute and from_atomic normalization of open bounds.
C.contract: New capability; tests fail because step/normalization did not exist.

B.label: bug
B.description: The sweep in IntervalDict.combine advanced through non-atomic keys by upper bound and could skip a later key filling an interior gap, dropping those points from the result.
B.contract: combine must cover the whole intersection of both domains; the sweep was introduced by an earlier commit (8db341e), so this is a regression.

C.label: bug
C.description: IntervalDict.combine sweep dropped pieces of the domain intersection for non-atomic keys.
C.contract: combine must cover the whole domain intersection.

B.label: bug
B.description: from_string tested infinity bounds with re.match, so a prefix match such as '-infinity' was silently treated as -inf instead of being rejected.
B.contract: A bound is infinite only if it matches the inf pattern entirely; otherwise it goes through conv, which raises for invalid text.

C.label: bug
C.description: from_string used re.match so partial matches such as "infinity" were accepted as infinity.
C.contract: Bounds must match the whole token.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds typing special cases so string arguments of assert_type, NewType, TypeVarTuple and ParamSpec are treated as annotations.
B.contract: These calls had no special handling; recognising their string arguments as annotations is new analysis capability.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds typing specializations treating assert_type/NewType/ParamSpec/TypeVarTuple arguments as annotations.
C.contract: New handling of additional typing constructs.

B.label: bug
B.description: Dict displays (and TypedDict dict arguments) were visited all keys first, then all values, so a walrus in a value used by a later key was reported as an undefined name.
B.contract: Python evaluates dict displays key, value, key, value in order (language reference); valid code must not get UndefinedName.

C.label: bug
C.description: Dict keys and values were handled keys-first rather than in interleaved evaluation order, breaking walrus uses.
C.contract: Python evaluates dict key then value pairwise.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds __debuggerskip__ to the special local names that are never reported as unused.
B.contract: The set of special IPython/traceback locals is a curated list; the commit adds a new entry.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds __debuggerskip__ as a recognized special local variable.
C.contract: New special-case name.

B.label: bug
B.description: The NamedTuple/TypedDict special-casing only visited the second argument when it was a literal list or dict, so a name passed there was never marked used and was reported as an unused import.
B.contract: pyflakes must not report a used import as unused; every argument expression of the call must be visited.

C.label: bug
C.description: NamedTuple/TypedDict handling assumed the second arg was a dict/list, wrongly treating non-literal args as annotations.
C.contract: Runtime-typed second arguments should not be handled as annotations.

B.label: bug
B.description: Reporter.syntaxError called max(lineno, 1) with lineno None, raising TypeError for tokenizer errors such as null bytes on Python 3.11.4+.
B.contract: pyflakes must report syntax errors instead of crashing.

C.label: bug
C.description: Reporter.syntaxError crashed with TypeError when lineno was None.
C.contract: Syntax errors from tokenization must be reportable.

B.label: bug
B.description: A walrus assignment after a bare annotation kept the Annotation binding via setdefault, so later uses of the name were reported as undefined.
B.contract: 'a: int; print(a := 3); print(a)' is valid code and must not produce UndefinedName.

C.label: bug
C.description: An assignment expression after a bare annotation did not replace the Annotation binding, giving false undefined-name reports.
C.contract: Walrus assignment defines the name.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends shebang detection to free-threaded interpreters such as python3.12t (and drops the m/u suffixes).
B.contract: The shebang regex never recognised the 't' suffix; the commit adds detection of a new interpreter naming.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Shebang detection now recognises python3t and drops python3m/pythonu suffixes.
C.contract: Deliberate update of recognised interpreter names.

B.label: bug
B.description: A walrus inside a comprehension replaced the existing binding of the same name in the enclosing scope, losing its used state and producing a false 'assigned but never used' warning.
B.contract: Reassigning an existing, used name (e.g. a parameter) via an assignment expression is valid and must not be reported.

C.label: bug
C.description: Assignment expressions inside generators overwrote outer bindings (e.g. a parameter) instead of reassigning, causing false reports.
C.contract: PEP 572 scoping: walrus rebinds the enclosing name.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Reports the actual syntax/decoding error with location instead of the generic 'problem decoding source' message.
B.contract: The F2P test only checks the new detailed message for a misencoded file; the old generic message was chosen deliberately and was not wrong for that case.

C.label: bug
C.description: Syntax errors from stdin were reported as decoding problems when text was None.
C.contract: Syntax errors should be reported with context.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The recorded failing test requires a more detailed encoding-error diagnostic in place of the accurate generic decoding-error message.
T.contract: Although the commit also repairs stdin syntax-error reporting, the sole recorded fail-to-pass test checks diagnostic enrichment for an actual encoding failure, not the repaired misclassification.

B.label: bug
B.description: With 'from __future__ import annotations', _in_postponed_annotation was true everywhere, so a bare annotation 'x: str' counted as a definition and later uses of x were not reported (the commit also adds Python 3.14 support).
B.contract: A bare annotation does not bind a name; using it outside an annotation is an undefined name with or without the future import.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds Python 3.14 support: t-strings and deferred annotation semantics.
C.contract: New language-version support.

T.label: bug
T.description: Enabling future annotations incorrectly treated ordinary name references as postponed annotations, suppressing undefined-name diagnostics.
T.contract: An annotation-only declaration does not assign a runtime value, and the failing future-annotations test requires UndefinedName for the subsequent print(x), independently of the added Python 3.14 support.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds handlers for PEP 695 TypeVarTuple (*T) and ParamSpec (**P) type parameters.
B.contract: These type-parameter node kinds had no handler; the commit adds support for them on top of the existing TypeVar support.

C.label: bug
C.description: PEP 695 ParamSpec and TypeVarTuple type params were not bound as names, causing false undefined-name reports.
C.contract: Valid 3.12 syntax should be handled.

T.label: feature
T.description: The commit extends type-parameter handling to PEP 695 TypeVarTuple and ParamSpec declarations.
T.contract: The packet shows existing handling for ordinary type parameters but no established promise covering these additional forms; the new tests exercise the added syntax support.

B.label: bug

B.label: bug

C.description: QuotedString stripped whitespace from quote delimiters, collapsing multi-character delimiters like "\n;".

B.label: bug
B.description: ParseResults.deepcopy wrote the copied sub-results into self._toklist instead of ret._toklist, mutating the original and leaving the copy sharing its contents.

C.label: bug
C.description: ParseResults.deepcopy modified self._toklist instead of the copy.

C.label: bug
C.description: ParseResults.copy shared per-name offset lists with the original so mutating the copy renumbered the original.
C.contract: Copy must be independent of the original.

B.label: bug
B.description: SkipTo kept its own ignoreExpr attribute and skipped only that, ignoring ignorable expressions registered through the grammar's ignore(), so it matched the target inside a comment.

C.label: bug
C.description: SkipTo stored ignore expressions separately and did not honor grammar-level ignores, matching targets inside comments.

B.label: bug
B.description: pyparsing_common.url regex was anchored with ^ and $, so it could only match a whole input string and failed inside larger grammars or lists of URLs.

C.label: bug
C.description: pp.common.url regex was anchored with ^ and $, preventing use inside larger grammars.
C.contract: URL expression should match within larger input (issue 459).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Escapes control characters in set_debug() output and adjusts the caret position.

C.label: bug

C.contract: Debug output must be readable (issue 496).

T.label: bug

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Deprecates ParserElement.validate() by emitting a DeprecationWarning.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Deprecates ParserElement.validate() by emitting DeprecationWarning.

B.label: bug
B.description: nested_expr's default content parse action used str.strip() with no argument, stripping all whitespace even when the default whitespace characters were set to '' so whitespace should be significant.

C.description: nested_expr evaluated its default ignore expression at definition time so changed default whitespace was not honored.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds rendering of stop_on lookahead for OneOrMore/ZeroOrMore in railroad diagrams.
C.contract: New diagram capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: match_previous_expr used e2.set_parse_action for the repeat check, which replaced the copied expression's own parse actions (e.g. integer conversion), so '1:1' with ppc.integer no longer matched.

C.label: bug
C.description: match_previous_expr replaced the wrapped repeater parse action instead of adding its own on the repeater, losing user parse actions.
C.contract: Parse actions on the expression must be preserved.

B.label: bug
B.description: match_previous_expr attached the must-match parse action to the Forward rep at parse time, which is lost when leave_whitespace(recursive=True) copies the sub-expressions, so '1:2' was accepted.

C.label: bug
C.description: match_previous_expr applied its must-match action to the wrong element, failing with recursive whitespace removal.
C.contract: match_previous_expr must reject non-matching repeats (issue 633).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Refactors Word to drop the internal _WordRegex class and __class__ reassignment; tests update the expected class name in explain() output.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Refactor removing __class__ assignment and _WordRegex class; test expectations updated.
C.contract: Internal refactor with test updates.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds slice notation expr[m, ...: stop_expr] to pass a stop_on sentinel in repetition indexing.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds slice notation expr[...:stop] for stop_on repetition.
C.contract: New syntax.

C.description: NotAny did not run the parse actions/conditions of its inner expression, so conditions were ignored.

C.label: bug
C.description: with_line_numbers omitted the header0 hundreds row for lines of 99+ chars and mis-ranged it.
C.contract: Output should include the column header for long lines.

B.label: feature

C.description: find_dotenv walked frames whose filename was inside a zip archive and failed with OSError when imported from a zipfile.
C.contract: Code imported from zip must not crash.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds support for reading .env from FIFOs.

C.label: bug
C.description: rewrite left a .tmp_ file behind and could mask the original error when cleanup failed on read-only files.
C.contract: Failed writes must not leak temp files or hide the real error.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds expansion of a leading ~ in dotenv_path for load_dotenv, dotenv_values, get_key, set_key, unset_key and the CLI --file option.

C.description: Adds --format option to the list command.

C.label: bug
C.description: rewrite referenced an undefined dest variable in the exception handler, raising UnboundLocalError.

C.label: bug
C.description: Invalid-line recovery regex tried "\r" before "\r\n", leaving a stray "\n" and breaking line numbering with CRLF.

C.description: A UTF-8 BOM at the start of a .env file was kept and became part of the first key, silently losing the variable.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: dotenv run now prints a friendly "Command not found" error and exits 1 instead of 2 (documented as breaking).

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: load_dotenv now returns False when no variables are found.

C.label: bug
C.description: dotenv get exited 1 for empty-string values because of a truthiness check.
C.contract: Empty string is a valid value (issue 699).

B.description: For 'KEY= # comment' the equal-sign regex consumed the whitespace before '#', so the inline comment was returned as the value instead of an empty string.

C.description: KEY= # comment parsed the comment text as the value instead of an empty string.

C.label: bug
C.description: set_key did not escape backslashes and the quoted-value regexes mis-handled escaped backslashes, breaking round-trips.
C.contract: Values written by set_key must read back identically.

C.label: bug
C.description: A trailing "**" translated to a bare "/" so it matched the parent directory itself.

B.label: bug

C.description: A lone "**" pattern compiled to ".+" which failed for GitIgnoreSpec (missing directory marker group).

C.description: A trailing "/*" pattern was rewritten to "/**" and trailing-segment handling differed, so '*' followed by '!dir/' re-includes mis-evaluated (issue 62).
C.contract: gitignore semantics: later negation of a directory must be respected.

C.description: Exclusion patterns ending without a slash did not match paths underneath the directory.

B.description: Double-asterisk path segments were translated with a plain '.', which does not match a newline, so '**' failed on file or directory names containing newlines.

C.description: Globstar and match-all regexes used "." without DOTALL so paths containing newlines did not match.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Simplifies the globstar regex fragments; tests only assert the changed regex text.
C.contract: Internal regex rewrite.

B.label: bug
B.description: GitIgnoreSpec's priority logic let an earlier file-pattern negation ('!*.txt') beat a later including directory pattern ('/test1/**'), leaving files in the ignored directory unignored.

C.label: bug
C.description: GitIgnoreSpec priority logic let a file exclude override an included directory pattern.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds __repr__ for PathSpec and RegexPattern and __str__ for RegexPattern.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds __repr__ for PathSpec/RegexPattern and __str__ for RegexPattern.

B.label: bug
B.description: PathSpec.match_file returned the internal tri-state include value, giving None instead of False for unmatched files.

C.label: bug
C.description: PathSpec.match_file could return None instead of a bool for unmatched files.

C.description: A bracket expression negated with ^ was escaped as a literal caret rather than negation as git does.

C.description: A pattern ending in "/*" matched only direct children, not all descendants as git does.

C.description: Collapses runs of consecutive asterisks into one wildcard in generated regex; matching semantics unchanged, tests check regex shape.

B.label: bug
B.description: GitWildMatchPattern stripped all surrounding whitespace, removing an escaped trailing space so patterns like '\\ ' or 'abc\\ ' raised GitWildMatchPatternError.

C.label: bug
C.description: Patterns ending with an escaped space were stripped of the trailing space, breaking git edge-case handling.

B.description: escape() did not escape trailing spaces, so the escaped pattern for a filename ending in a space had the space stripped by gitignore parsing and no longer matched that file.
