C.label: bug
C.description: escape() did not escape trailing spaces so an escaped filename ending with a space no longer matched.
C.contract: Git strips unescaped trailing spaces; escape() should produce a pattern matching the literal file.

B.label: bug
B.description: Comparison operators passed malformed dict/tuple/list operands straight to Version construction, so '==' raised ValueError/TypeError from __init__ instead of returning NotImplemented (False for equality).
B.contract: The library's documented policy for invalid comparison operands is to return NotImplemented; equality with a non-version operand should evaluate to False, not raise.

C.label: bug
C.description: Comparing Version with malformed dict/tuple/list leaks ValueError/TypeError from __init__ instead of returning NotImplemented.
C.contract: Library policy for invalid comparison operands is NotImplemented (changelog gh 316).

B.label: bug
B.description: Version.replace caught the constructor's TypeError and always re-raised it as 'replace() got 0 unexpected keyword argument(s)', hiding the real type error.
B.contract: The custom message is only correct for unknown keywords; for known keys with bad values it was a wrong, misleading message.

C.label: bug
C.description: Version.replace replaced a constructor TypeError with a misleading "0 unexpected keyword arguments" error.
C.contract: Original constructor TypeError should be preserved when no unknown keys exist.

B.label: bug
B.description: The comparator wrapper accepted any Version instance, so comparing a subclass instance with a base Version called compare() and raised TypeError instead of returning NotImplemented and deferring to the reflected operation.
B.contract: Equality between a Version subclass instance and an equal base Version should work (evaluate True), not raise.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Comparison type check changed from Version to type(self), altering subclass/base comparison semantics.
C.contract: Tests assert deliberate new TypeError/NotImplemented asymmetry for subclasses.

T.label: bug
T.description: The comparison wrapper accepted a base Version operand for a subclass whose compare method rejected it, raising TypeError before reflected comparison could succeed.
T.contract: The existing compare restriction is demonstrated by the test's expected TypeError, while rich comparison must return NotImplemented for unsupported operands so the compatible base-class comparison can handle equality.

B.label: bug
B.description: Prerelease comparison converted numeric identifiers with int(), which raises ValueError for identifiers longer than Python's 4300-digit conversion limit even though such versions parse as valid.
B.contract: Version.is_valid/parse accept the version, so comparing it must not crash; SemVer orders numeric identifiers numerically.

C.label: bug
C.description: Comparing very long numeric prerelease identifiers raised ValueError due to int conversion limit.
C.contract: Valid versions must be comparable.

B.label: bug
B.description: The version regex used '$' and Unicode-aware digit matching, so strings with a trailing newline or non-ASCII digits were accepted by parse() and is_valid().
B.contract: SemVer allows only ASCII digits and no trailing characters; is_valid('1.2.3\n') returning True is a wrong result.

C.label: bug
C.description: Version regex accepted trailing newline ($) and non-ASCII digits.
C.contract: SemVer grammar permits only ASCII digits and no trailing characters.

B.label: bug
B.description: next_version interpolated the prerelease token into a regex unescaped and compared only the first dot-separated part, so tokens with '.' or regex characters mismatched (alphaXbeta9 matched alpha.beta, alpha.beta.1 was reset) or crashed with a PatternError.
B.contract: The token must be matched literally as a prerelease prefix; the commit also adds new validation of invalid tokens.

C.label: bug
C.description: Prerelease token used unescaped in a regex and matched by first dotted component, mis-matching multi-part tokens.
C.contract: Token must be matched literally and validated.

B.label: bug
B.description: next_version treated build-only versions like prereleases and only stripped the build, so 1.2.3+build.5 bumped to 1.2.3 instead of 1.2.4.
B.contract: next_version must return the next version in precedence; build metadata does not affect precedence, so returning an equal version is wrong.

C.label: bug
C.description: next_version treated build-only versions as prerelease and only stripped build instead of bumping.
C.contract: Build metadata does not affect precedence; patch bump must increment.

B.label: bug
B.description: The old-style prerelease branch of next_version called replace() without build=None, so build metadata survived while every other path dropped it.
B.contract: next_version('prerelease') drops build metadata on all other paths (1.2.3-rc.1+build.5 becomes 1.2.3-rc.2).

C.label: bug
C.description: Bumping an old-style prerelease kept build metadata unlike all other prerelease bump paths.
C.contract: next_version("prerelease") drops build.

B.label: bug
B.description: next_version('prerelease') on old-style prereleases like 'rc3' reset to 'rc.1' instead of incrementing, yielding a version lower than the input.
B.contract: next_version is meant to produce the next greater version; 0.1.2-rc.1 sorts before 0.1.2-rc3 (issue #484).

C.label: bug
C.description: next_version("prerelease") reset old-style prereleases such as rc3 to rc.1 instead of incrementing.
C.contract: Issue 484: rc3 should bump to rc4.

B.label: bug
B.description: next_version('prerelease') on an old-style counter like 'rc9' returned '1.2.3-rc10', which sorts lower than '1.2.3-rc9' under SemVer's lexical ordering.
B.contract: next_version is meant to return a greater version than the input; going backwards breaks version ordering.

C.label: bug
C.description: next_version on legacy prerelease counters like rc9 produced rc10, which sorts lower than rc9.
C.contract: next_version must not return a version lower than the input.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds support for match expressions without an operator, defaulting to equality.
B.contract: New accepted input form; the old test expected ValueError for '1.0.0' and the new tests fail only because the default did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: match() now accepts a bare version as equality match.
C.contract: New capability; previously raised ValueError by design.

B.label: bug
B.description: Switching to a prerelease token that sorts earlier (rc to alpha) returned a version older than the input, e.g. 1.2.3-rc.1 to 1.2.3-alpha.1.
B.contract: next_version must not move backwards in SemVer order (issue #497).

C.label: bug
C.description: Switching to an earlier-sorting prerelease token returned a version lower than the input.
C.contract: next_version result must be greater than input (issue 497).

B.label: bug
B.description: Version.replace constructed a hard-coded Version instead of type(self), so subclasses lost their type (and custom __str__) after replace().
B.contract: The documentation's 'Creating Subclasses from Version' example expects replace() on a subclass to return that subclass (issue #426).

C.label: bug
C.description: replace() always built a base Version, losing the subclass.
C.contract: Subclass overriding construction should be preserved by replace (issue 426).

B.label: bug
B.description: bump_build() returned an unchanged version when the build metadata contained no digits (e.g. 1.2.3+alpha), because _increment_string left it as is.
B.contract: bump_build is documented to raise the build part and return a new version; returning the same build silently violates that (mirrors prerelease fix #460).

C.label: bug
C.description: bump_build on digitless build metadata returns an unchanged version.
C.contract: Bumping must raise the build part; mirrors prerelease fix 460.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds support for lists of dataclass instances as tabular data.
B.contract: New supported input type documented by this commit; tests fail only because dataclasses were not handled.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds support for lists of dataclasses as input.
C.contract: New input type.

B.label: bug
B.description: With intfmt set, string cells detected as integers (e.g. '1500' or ANSI-colored numbers) were passed to format() with the int format spec, raising ValueError.
B.contract: Numeric strings are valid table cells and are classified as ints; using intfmt must not crash (issue #318).

C.label: bug
C.description: intfmt crashed with ValueError for string values holding integers.
C.contract: intfmt should work for integer-valued strings (issue 318).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Replaces the deprecated align="..." attributes in the mediawiki format with style="text-align: ...;".
B.contract: The old markup was deprecated but still valid; tests are updated to the new markup.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Mediawiki alignment attributes switched from deprecated align= to style=text-align.
C.contract: Deliberate update to HTML5-compliant output.

B.label: bug
B.description: maxcolwidths handling indexed list_of_lists[0] on empty data and raised IndexError.
B.contract: tabulate([]) returns an empty string; adding maxcolwidths must not make empty input crash (issue #180).

C.label: bug
C.description: Empty data with maxcolwidths raised IndexError.
C.contract: Empty table is valid input (issue 180).

B.label: feature
B.description: Accepts unsized (infinite) iterables such as generators as showindex row indices, consuming only as many values as there are rows.
B.contract: The index previously had to match the number of rows (len(index) was checked), so infinite iterables were never supported.

C.label: bug
C.description: Row index iterables were consumed via len/list and failed for infinite iterators.
C.contract: showindex documented to accept an iterable; issue 175 reports failure.

T.label: bug
T.description: Row-index normalization eagerly exhausted an iterable instead of consuming only the indices needed for the table.
T.contract: The existing showindex branch accepts Iterable values, and a finite table needs only one index per data row; the regression test detects excessive consumption.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Strips trailing whitespace from asciidoc rows.
B.contract: The old tests explicitly expected the trailing padding and it did not change how the table renders, so this is a cosmetic output change despite the 'fix' wording.

C.label: bug
C.description: asciidoc output had trailing whitespace on lines.
C.contract: Issue 408 reports unwanted trailing whitespace.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The commit removes trailing padding from AsciiDoc output as a formatting cleanup.
T.contract: Existing tests explicitly included trailing spaces, and the packet establishes neither a prior whitespace prohibition nor incorrect AsciiDoc rendering.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds the intfmt parameter (and CLI option) for formatting integer columns.
B.contract: New parameter; the signature test fails only because it did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds the intfmt parameter.
C.contract: New option.

B.label: bug
B.description: Decimal values were converted to float before applying floatfmt, losing precision (e.g. 99999998999.999980 was misprinted).
B.contract: tabulate formats Decimal values as numbers; the printed value must reflect the given Decimal, not a float approximation (issue #176).

C.label: bug
C.description: Decimal values were converted to float before formatting, losing precision with floatfmt.
C.contract: Decimal values should be formatted exactly (issue 176).

B.label: bug
B.description: With maxcolwidths, each cell was passed whole to TextWrapper.wrap, which replaces newlines with spaces, so explicit line breaks in cells were lost.
B.contract: tabulate supports multiline cells; wrapping to a maximum width should not merge existing lines (issue #190).

C.label: bug
C.description: Wrapping text with maxcolwidths discarded existing line breaks in cells.
C.contract: Explicit newlines in cells should be preserved (issue 190).

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Makes the 'github' format an alias of 'pipe', so its separator row now carries alignment colons.
B.contract: The previous 'github' output without colons was deliberate and asserted by existing tests; the tests are updated to the new policy.

C.label: bug
C.description: github table format omitted alignment colons in the separator row.
C.contract: GitHub markdown tables should honor column alignment (issue 53).

T.label: bug
T.description: GitHub tables omitted separator alignment markers, so rendered Markdown did not honor column alignment.
T.contract: The existing alignment options and numeric alignment behavior should be reflected in the selected output format; the explicit colalign test demonstrates the violation.

B.label: bug
B.description: With maxheadercolwidths, tabulate indexed list_of_lists[0] without checking for empty data and raised IndexError.
B.contract: An empty table with headers is valid input and renders headers only (issue #365); the analogous maxcolwidths case was already fixed.

C.label: bug
C.description: maxheadercolwidths with empty data indexed list_of_lists[0] and raised IndexError.
C.contract: Empty table with headers is valid input (issue 365).

B.label: bug
B.description: SEPARATING_LINE detection compared the raw cell value exactly, so it failed when the value had been padded, and the separator was not drawn in padded formats like psql.
B.contract: The SEPARATING_LINE feature should work regardless of column padding (issue #231).

C.label: bug
C.description: SEPARATING_LINE was not detected once padded by column formatting.
C.contract: Separating line must work with padded-column formats (issue 231).

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds the maxheadercolwidths parameter to wrap header cells.
B.contract: New parameter; the signature test fails only because it did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds maxheadercolwidths parameter.
C.contract: New option.

B.label: bug
B.description: For empty data with headers='firstrow', the literal string 'firstrow' stayed as headers and was split into one-letter column headers.
B.contract: headers='firstrow' means use the first data row as headers; with no rows the table must be empty, not show 'f','i','r',... headers.

C.label: bug
C.description: Empty data with headers=firstrow did not yield an empty table.
C.contract: Empty table should render as empty string.

B.label: bug
B.description: The asciidoc column specifiers were emitted as width-then-alignment ('11<') instead of AsciiDoc's alignment-then-width ('<11'), so alignments were not applied.
B.contract: AsciiDoc's cols syntax puts the alignment operator before the width.

C.label: bug
C.description: asciidoc column specifier had width and alignment in the wrong order.
C.contract: AsciiDoc cols syntax is alignment then width, e.g. <11.

B.label: bug
B.description: The pipe/github row format was built without an escape map, so a '|' inside a cell was emitted unescaped and broke the Markdown table structure.
B.contract: The existing regression test for issue #241 requires the github format to escape '|' as '\|'; unescaped pipes produce extra columns.

C.label: bug
C.description: Pipe characters in cells were not escaped in github/pipe formats, breaking the table.
C.contract: Regression test for issue 241 requires escaping pipe with backslash.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends dict-row handling to dict-like objects such as UserDict by duck-typing keys/values.
B.contract: Only dict rows were documented as supported; this adds a new accepted input type.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds support for lists of dict-like objects such as UserDict.
C.contract: New accepted input type.

B.label: bug
B.description: The moinmoin left-alignment attribute was the HTML-style ' style="text-align: left;"' instead of moinmoin's '<style="text-align: left;">', producing malformed cell markup.
B.contract: moinmoin cell attributes use the '<style=...>' syntax already used for right/center alignment; the output must be valid moinmoin markup.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: moinmoin and html output now emit explicit left-alignment style.
C.contract: Test expectations updated to add explicit text-align left; no prior promise broken.

T.label: bug
T.description: The MoinMoin left-alignment attribute lacked the angle brackets required by the cell-style syntax.
T.contract: The existing left-alignment mapping should produce valid markup, consistent with the right, center, and decimal mappings; the failing tests exercise this correction.

B.label: bug
B.description: SEPARATING_LINE rows were padded and rendered as data rows in formats with padding or linebetweenrows (e.g. grid) instead of being drawn as separator lines.
B.contract: SEPARATING_LINE is an existing feature that must render a separator line in every table format (issues #322/#328).

C.label: bug
C.description: SEPARATING_LINE rows were padded or rendered as data rows in padded/linebetweenrows formats.
C.contract: Separating lines are a supported feature that must work across formats (issues 322, 328).

B.label: bug
B.description: Passing maxcolwidths as a tuple crashed with TypeError because the code concatenated it with a list.
B.contract: maxcolwidths is a per-column sequence; a tuple is a natural valid value (issue #214), like for colalign.

C.label: bug
C.description: A tuple for maxcolwidths raised TypeError on list concatenation.
C.contract: maxcolwidths documented to accept list or tuple (issue 214).

B.label: bug
B.description: Constant-folding of exception tuples built argument strings including trailing comments, so duplicates with a comment were not deduplicated and a comment could land inline before '):', commenting out the rest of the line.
B.contract: pyupgrade rewrites must produce valid, equivalent code; 'except (A, B # b): ...' is broken output (issue #932).

C.label: bug
C.description: Constant folding of exception tuples included comments in argument text, producing wrong dedupe and broken output.
C.contract: Comments are not part of the argument; issue 932.

B.label: bug
B.description: The default-encoding fix searched for the first '(' token, which with Python 3.12 f-string tokenization could be inside an f-string placeholder, deleting the wrong call's arguments.
B.contract: Removing a redundant .encode('utf-8') argument must not alter other code; corrupting f"{foo(bar)}" is wrong output.

C.label: bug
C.description: Finding the encode call matched a paren inside an f-string placeholder, corrupting output.
C.contract: Rewrite must remove encode args only.

B.label: bug
B.description: Unquoting a string annotation replaced only the first STRING token, so implicitly concatenated multi-line annotations left the remaining string tokens behind and produced wrong code.
B.contract: Dequoting an annotation must replace the whole string expression with its unquoted form.

C.label: bug
C.description: Unstringing implicit-concatenated multiline annotations left remaining string tokens.
C.contract: Rewrite must produce valid unquoted annotation.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends PEP 563 annotation unquoting to async function definitions.
B.contract: Leaving async annotations quoted was valid code; the rewrite's scope is broadened.

C.label: feature
C.description: PEP 563 rewrite extended to async functions.
C.contract: New rewrite coverage.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds the --py314-plus option and Python 3.14-specific rewrites (e.g. unquoting annotations without the __future__ import).
B.contract: New target-version capability; the test fails only because 3.14 support did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds Python 3.14 support: new flag and rewrite behaviours.
C.contract: New --py314-plus option and rules.

B.label: bug
B.description: unittest.makeSuite and similar deprecated helpers were rewritten to loader methods even with extra positional or keyword arguments those methods do not accept.
B.contract: A rewrite must keep the call valid; loadTestsFromTestCase(Tests, 'arg') fails where makeSuite(Tests, 'arg') worked.

C.label: bug
C.description: unittest alias rewrite applied to calls with extra args or keywords, changing semantics.
C.contract: Rewrite only valid for single-argument calls.

B.label: feature
B.description: Allows deleting dead versioned if blocks without else at module scope.
B.contract: The previous behaviour deliberately skipped these blocks; this is a new rewrite.

C.label: feature
C.description: Dead versioned if without else is now removed at module scope.
C.contract: Previously deliberately skipped.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds rewriting of versioned branches followed by elif, which was previously skipped on purpose.
B.contract: Old tests documented 'for now we don't attempt to rewrite elif'; this extends the rewrite.

C.label: feature
C.description: Versioned-branch rewrite now handles elif chains.
C.contract: Previously elif was explicitly not attempted.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds PEP 563 unquoting for Python 3.12+ TypeVar bounds.
B.contract: New syntax support; the test fails only because TypeVar bounds were not visited before.

C.label: feature
C.description: PEP 563 rewrite extended to 3.12 TypeVar bounds.
C.contract: New rewrite coverage.

B.label: bug
B.description: The shlex.join rewrite accepted any string separator, so '"wat".join(shlex.quote(arg) ...)' was rewritten to shlex.join(cmd), which joins with a space.
B.contract: shlex.join is only equivalent to ' '.join(shlex.quote(...)); other separators change behaviour.

C.label: bug
C.description: shlex.join rewrite applied to any string separator instead of only a space.
C.contract: Rewrite must preserve semantics.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends the io.open-to-open rewrite to non-call references such as 'x = io.open'.
B.contract: Leaving io.open references untouched was valid code; this broadens the rewrite's coverage.

C.label: feature
C.description: io.open is now replaced by open also when not directly called.
C.contract: Extends rewrite coverage; previous behavior merely missed the case.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds rewriting of typing.Unpack in *args annotations to the star syntax for Python 3.11+.
B.contract: New rewrite; the test fails only because *args annotations were not handled yet.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds rewrite of Unpack to star in *args annotations.
C.contract: New rewrite rule.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends the identity_equality rewrite (x is <literal> to x == <literal>) to complex literals.
B.contract: Adds a literal type to the rewrite's scope; the test fails only because complex was not covered yet.

C.label: feature
C.description: identity_equality rewrite now also covers complex literals.
C.contract: Extends supported literal types; previously not rewritten.

B.label: bug
B.description: The TYPE_CHECKING-to-lazy-import rewrite also fired on if TYPE_CHECKING blocks inside functions, producing 'lazy from ...' imports where they are not allowed.
B.contract: Lazy imports are only valid at module scope, so pyupgrade must not emit them in function bodies (the output would not be valid code).

C.label: bug
C.description: TYPE_CHECKING blocks were rewritten inside functions, not only at module scope.
C.contract: Rewrite is only valid for module-scope blocks; tests mark nested as noop.

B.label: feature
B.description: Teaches the always-true/always-false version analysis to recognize 'and'/'or' compound conditions.
B.contract: Extends which version checks are rewritten; leaving compound conditions untouched was the previous, safe behaviour.

C.label: feature
C.description: Version-branch simplification now understands and/or bool ops.
C.contract: New capability; old code left such branches untouched.

B.label: feature
B.description: Extends the empty set literal rewrite to calls with whitespace before the parenthesis, e.g. 'set (())'.
B.contract: The old code deliberately skipped this case (TODO, and an explicit noop test); leaving it untouched was valid.

C.label: feature
C.description: set literal empty rewrite now handles unusual whitespace like set (()), previously deliberately skipped.
C.contract: Old test listed it as a noop; now supported.

B.label: bug
B.description: dict()/set() calls directly inside an f-string placeholder were rewritten to literals, yielding '{{...}}', which is an escaped brace and changes the string's meaning.
B.contract: pyupgrade rewrites must preserve semantics; f"{dict(...)}" must not become literal brace text.

C.label: bug
C.description: dict/set call directly in an f-string placeholder was rewritten to a brace form that breaks the f-string.
C.contract: Rewrite must preserve valid output.

B.label: bug
B.description: parse_call_args counted a trailing comment-only segment after the last comma as an argument, causing 'too many values to unpack' when rewriting calls like itertools.chain(x, # comment).
B.contract: Comments are not call arguments; pyupgrade must not crash on valid source with a trailing comment.

C.label: bug
C.description: parse_call_args counted a trailing comment-only segment as an argument.
C.contract: Comments are not arguments; crash in itertools.chain rewrite.

B.label: bug
B.description: parse_format merged a named unicode escape (\N{...}) into the previous part even when that part held a replacement field, dropping the '{}' placeholder.
B.contract: Format-string handling must preserve placeholders; the format_literals plugin must leave '"{}\N{SNOWMAN}".format("")' unchanged.

C.label: bug
C.description: parse_format merged a named unicode escape into a preceding placeholder part, corrupting format rewrite.
C.contract: Format specifier must not be touched; test shows output dropped the placeholder.

B.label: bug
B.description: is_name_attr was given the string 'ArgumentParser' instead of a tuple, so substring membership matched other names like 'ArgumentPar' and dropped their suggest_on_error argument.
B.contract: The rewrite must apply only to argparse.ArgumentParser; altering an unrelated call changes program behaviour.

C.label: bug
C.description: A string instead of a tuple was passed as names, so substring matching rewrote unrelated names like ArgumentPar.
C.contract: Only argparse.ArgumentParser should be rewritten.

B.label: bug
B.description: The literal check used 'n.value not in {True, False}', and since 1 == True and 0.0 == False, int/float literals 0, 1, 0.0, 1.0 were wrongly skipped.
B.contract: The plugin rewrites 'x is <int/float literal>'; only real bools are meant to be excluded.

C.label: bug
C.description: Literal check used set membership so 1 and 1.0 were treated as booleans and skipped.
C.contract: Ints/floats equal to True/False must still be rewritten.

B.label: bug
B.description: _cell_len called next() on the character iterator after a zero-width joiner without checking for end of input, so a trailing ZWJ raised StopIteration; control characters were also measured as one cell instead of zero.
B.contract: cell_len must return a width for any string, including '\u200d' or '1\u200d', instead of raising; non-printable control characters occupy no cells.

C.label: bug
C.description: cell width lookup crashed with StopIteration and mishandled ZWJ and control chars.
C.contract: Control chars have zero width and lookup must not crash.

B.label: bug
B.description: Markdown rendering yielded a new-line segment before inline elements as well as block elements, adding superfluous blank lines and spaces, e.g. in tables with empty cells.
B.contract: Inline content belongs on the same line as its parent block; the extra new lines are spurious output, which the commit title names a superfluous-space fix.

C.label: bug
C.description: Markdown rendering inserted a superfluous newline/space for inline elements (e.g. in tables with empty cells).
C.contract: Table output should not contain extra blank space.

B.label: bug
B.description: Segment._split_cells estimated a start position and walked only forward, so for some mixed single/double-width strings the left part did not have exactly 'cut' cells.
B.contract: split_cells must split a segment at the given cell column so that the left part has cell length equal to the cut; this broke layout in Textual (textual#4996).

C.label: bug
C.description: Segment.split_cells produced wrong cell widths for mixed-width text.
C.contract: Split must land on the requested cell position.

B.label: bug
B.description: Inspect used getattr(obj, '__qualname__') unchecked, so an object whose __qualname__ is not a string (e.g. a slot descriptor on an lru_cache-wrapped class) made Text concatenation raise 'Only str or Text can be appended to Text'.
B.contract: rich.inspect should render any Python object without raising; the object here is valid and only has an unusual __qualname__ attribute.

C.label: bug
C.description: inspect failed for classes with a non-str __qualname__.
C.contract: inspect should handle unusual __qualname__.

B.label: bug
B.description: Syntax rendered its padding with the theme's background style instead of the effective base style, so a background_color override did not extend to the padded area.
B.contract: background_color overrides the theme background for the whole Syntax block, and padding is part of that block (issue #3295).

C.label: bug
C.description: Syntax padding used the theme background instead of the overridden background color.
C.contract: Padding should use the effective background (issue 3295).

B.label: bug
B.description: Style.clear_meta_and_links copied the source style's cached _hash into the new style even though links and meta were removed, leaving the copy with a stale hash.
B.contract: A Style's hash must reflect its own attributes so equal styles hash equally and style caches stay correct (issue #2942).

C.label: bug
C.description: Style.clear_meta_and_links copied the cached hash, so the cleared style hashed as the original.
C.contract: Hash must reflect cleared style (issue 2942).

B.label: bug
B.description: FileProxy, which stands in for stdout/stderr during live displays, inherited io.TextIOBase.isatty() and always returned False instead of forwarding to the wrapped file.
B.contract: FileProxy is meant to be a transparent proxy for the real file (it already forwards fileno); issue #4041 reports the wrong isatty result as a regression.

C.label: bug
C.description: FileProxy did not proxy isatty so wrapped TTY streams reported false.
C.contract: File proxy should delegate file methods (issue 4041).

B.label: bug
B.description: Text.append_tokens appended token content without stripping control codes (unlike Text.append), so a '\r' inside a token left spans and text out of step and wrapping raised IndexError.
B.contract: Text methods that add content strip control codes so offsets stay consistent; printing the result of append_tokens should not raise (issue #3014).

C.label: bug
C.description: append_tokens did not strip control codes and caused IndexError.
C.contract: Text should not contain control codes (issue 3014).

B.label: bug
B.description: Panel stylized its title and subtitle with only the border style instead of the combined panel+border style, so the panel's background was missing behind the title text.
B.contract: The panel's style (e.g. 'on blue') applies to the whole panel including its border line, so the title embedded in the border should share that background (issue #3569).

C.label: bug
C.description: Panel title and subtitle used only the partial border style and lost the panel background.
C.contract: Title should carry the panel background (issue 2745).

B.label: feature
B.description: Console reads a new TTY_INTERACTIVE environment variable ('0'/'1') to force interactive mode off or on when force_interactive is not given.
B.contract: No such environment variable was recognised before; the test fails only because the new override did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds TTY_INTERACTIVE environment variable support.
C.contract: New configuration capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: AnsiDecoder.decode split its input with str.splitlines(), which drops a trailing line break and so collapses trailing and lone newlines, making Text.from_ansi('\n').plain '' and 'Hello\n' come back as 'Hello'.
B.contract: Text.from_ansi should reproduce the input's plain text with only escape sequences removed; issue #3577 reports the lost newlines and the new test is a regression test for it.

C.label: bug
C.description: AnsiDecoder.decode used splitlines and lost trailing-newline information.
C.contract: Decoding should preserve newlines.

B.label: bug
B.description: The ANSI-decoding regex did not match two-character private escape sequences such as ESC 7 / ESC 8 (ESC followed by 0-9, :, ;, <, =, >, ?), so Text.from_ansi left raw escape characters in the text and they leaked into printed output.
B.contract: Text.from_ansi is meant to strip or interpret terminal escape sequences and yield clean text; unrecognised sequences corrupted the printed output.

C.label: bug
C.description: ANSI regex did not strip private escape sequences ESC followed by 0-?.
C.contract: Problematic private sequences should be removed when decoding.

B.label: bug
B.description: When add_row created columns implicitly, it constructed Column(_index=index) without passing the table's highlight setting, so those columns were never highlighted.
B.contract: Table(highlight=True) applies highlighting to its columns; columns created by add_row should behave like those created by add_column (issue #3517).

C.label: bug
C.description: Columns created by add_row did not inherit table highlight.
C.contract: Table highlight should apply to all columns (issue 3517).

B.label: bug
B.description: Console.print with no objects always rendered a NewLine and ignored the end argument, so print(end='!') wrote '\n' instead of '!'.
B.contract: The documented end parameter is the string written at the end of the output, mirroring builtin print where print(end='!') writes just '!'.

C.label: bug
C.description: console.print() with no objects and a custom end still printed a newline.
C.contract: end parameter should be honored for empty print.

B.label: bug
B.description: Table._get_padding_width ignored pad_edge=False (and mis-handled collapse_padding), so column measurements included edge padding that is never rendered and tables/columns came out with extra trailing spaces.
B.contract: With pad_edge=False the outer columns have no edge padding, so measured widths must match the rendered cells; the output 'aaa aaa aaa ' had a spurious trailing space.

C.label: bug
C.description: Table padding width miscomputed with collapse_padding.
C.contract: Column widths must account correctly for padding.

B.label: bug
B.description: Table rendering listed the box segment tuples as head, foot, mid while indexing them as head, mid, foot, so body rows were drawn with footer edge characters and the last row with mid characters.
B.contract: Each row type should use its own Box characters (mid_* for body rows, foot_* for the footer); custom boxes with distinct characters exposed the swap.

C.label: bug
C.description: Table box element order placed foot before mid, rendering wrong borders.
C.contract: Table border rows must use correct element placement.

B.label: bug
B.description: PromptBase.on_validate_error printed the error with the console's markup setting, so on a Console(markup=False) the internal '[prompt.invalid]' markup was printed literally.
B.contract: Prompt validation errors are built with rich markup by the library itself and should render as styled text whatever the console's markup default.

C.label: bug
C.description: Prompt error printed raw markup when console markup was disabled.
C.contract: Error markup should be rendered.

B.label: bug
B.description: The fast-path regex _is_single_cell_widths had wrong range bounds ('\u0020-\u006f' instead of up to '\u007e', and a missing dash in '\u00a0\u02ff'), so common single-width characters such as 'p'..'~' were not recognised.
B.contract: The regex is documented as matching the most common single-cell character ranges, and every printable ASCII character is single-width; the commit also adds box-drawing characters to the ranges.

C.label: bug
C.description: Single-cell width regex had wrong character ranges (e.g. 0x6f..0xa0 gap), mis-classifying characters.
C.contract: Regex must match exactly the single-cell ranges.

B.label: bug
B.description: Syntax computed the code width for wrapping from the full available width without subtracting the horizontal padding, so padded, word-wrapped code was laid out too wide and wrapped at the wrong place.
B.contract: padding and word_wrap are documented Syntax options and the padded output must fit the console width; issue #3727 reports the broken wrap.

C.label: bug
C.description: Syntax padding was not accounted for when wrapping, producing wrong wrapped output.
C.contract: Wrapped code must respect padding width.

B.label: bug
B.description: ReprHighlighter's URL regex character class lacked '@', so URL highlighting stopped at the first '@' in a path such as 'https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips'.
B.contract: '@' is a legal URL path character and the highlighter should cover the whole URL; issue #3327 reports the broken highlighting.

C.label: bug
C.description: URL highlight regex omitted the @ character.
C.contract: URLs with @ must be fully highlighted (issue 3327).

B.label: bug
B.description: Segment._split_cells estimated its starting character position as int(cut / cell_length * (len(text) - 1)), which can overshoot the cut for mixed-width text; the following loop only walks forward, so the left part ended up wider than the requested cut.
B.contract: split_cells must split at the given cell column so the left part's cell length equals the cut (textual#4996); the commit makes the estimate conservative so the forward scan can reach the cut.

C.label: bug
C.description: split_cells estimated split position incorrectly for mixed-width text.
C.contract: Cell split must be exact.

B.label: bug
B.description: Console._check_buffer copied the buffer into the record buffer even while a capture was active, so with record=True every nested buffer check re-recorded the captured lines and export_text returned duplicated output.
B.contract: export_text must not contain repeated copies of printed lines (issue #2563); the fix also excludes captured output from the record, which the new test pins.

C.label: bug
C.description: Record buffer was extended during capture, duplicating output.
C.contract: Capture and record should not duplicate prints.

B.label: bug
B.description: Live.stop always emitted a newline on terminals, even when the live render had produced zero lines, so a Live with an empty renderable left a stray blank line.
B.contract: A Live display that rendered nothing (especially with transient=True) should leave no output behind; issue #3796 reports the extra newline.

C.label: bug
C.description: Empty Live display still emitted a newline on stop.
C.contract: Empty live should not emit output lines.

B.label: bug
B.description: get_character_cell_size returned 0 for codepoints beyond the last entry of the width table, so private-use glyphs such as Nerd Font icons were measured as zero-width.
B.contract: Unlisted printable codepoints default to a width of 1 (the lookup's own fallback for gaps returns 1); issue #3943 reports the misaligned output.

C.label: bug
C.description: Characters beyond the width table returned 0 cells instead of 1.
C.contract: Unallocated characters like nerd-font glyphs occupy 1 cell (issue 3943).

B.label: bug
B.description: Progress.stop printed a newline for non-interactive consoles even when the progress display was disabled, so a disabled progress still produced output.
B.contract: Progress(disable=True) should produce no output at all (an existing test asserts this for the interactive case).

C.label: bug
C.description: Disabled Progress.stop still printed a blank line.
C.contract: Disabled progress should produce no output.

B.label: bug
B.description: strip_whitespace did not remove trailing whitespace inside the last subgroup of a parenthesis, leaving '(where foo = bar )'.
B.contract: strip_whitespace removes superfluous whitespace, including before a closing parenthesis (issue #782).

C.label: bug
C.description: strip_whitespace left trailing whitespace inside nested groups.
C.contract: Whitespace stripping should descend into subgroups (issue 782).

B.label: bug
B.description: The statement splitter split on semicolons inside BEGIN...END bodies outside CREATE statements (e.g. WITH FUNCTION ... BEGIN ... END), breaking one statement into fragments.
B.contract: Semicolons inside a BEGIN...END block do not terminate the enclosing statement (issue #809).

C.label: bug
C.description: Semicolons inside BEGIN...END blocks split the statement.
C.contract: Block body must stay in one statement (issue 809).

B.label: bug
B.description: Grouping could pull a group's own delimiter tokens into inner groups, and the aligned-indent and strip-whitespace filters assumed END or parentheses were present, so format() raised IndexError/ValueError on malformed SQL.
B.contract: sqlparse is a non-validating parser; format() should return a string for any input rather than crash.

C.label: bug
C.description: Grouping absorbed delimiter tokens into inner groups, making format crash with IndexError on malformed SQL.
C.contract: format should not raise on malformed input.

B.label: bug
B.description: 'PRIMARY KEY' was lexed as two separate keyword tokens instead of a single multi-word keyword.
B.contract: The commit fixes a reported parsing issue (#740), consistent with other multi-word keywords like 'GROUP BY'; the user-visible impact is not shown, hence low confidence.

C.label: bug
C.description: PRIMARY KEY was tokenized as two separate keywords.
C.contract: Compound keyword should be one token (issue 740).

B.label: bug
B.description: The Python and PHP output formatters escaped quotes but not backslashes, so a backslash before a quote could break out of the generated string literal.
B.contract: Generated string literals must reproduce the SQL text exactly (security advisory GHSA-3496-9g83-7v6x).

C.label: bug
C.description: Python and PHP output formatters did not escape backslashes, allowing breakout from the string literal.
C.contract: Generated literal must be faithful; security advisory GHSA-3496-9g83-7v6x.

B.label: bug
B.description: The statement splitter treated BEGIN TRANSACTION as the start of a BEGIN...END block, so a whole transaction script came back as a single statement.
B.contract: sqlparse.split must split 'BEGIN TRANSACTION; ...; END TRANSACTION;' into its separate statements (issue #826).

C.label: bug
C.description: BEGIN TRANSACTION was treated as a block start so subsequent statements were not split.
C.contract: Splitting must separate transaction statements (issue 826).

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds a new sql.Over group for window OVER clauses and attaches it to the preceding Function.
B.contract: New grouping class and behaviour; the test fails because OVER clauses were not modelled before.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds OVER clause grouping into Function.
C.contract: New grammar support.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds lexer support for PostgreSQL JSON operators such as '->', '->>', '#>', '@>' and '<@'.
B.contract: New supported syntax; tests fail only because these operators were not recognized as single tokens.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds tokenization of JSON operators.
C.contract: New supported syntax.

B.label: feature
B.description: Treats the Transact-SQL batch separator GO (optionally 'GO n') as a statement splitter.
B.contract: GO is a client-tool separator rather than SQL; supporting it extends the splitter to a new dialect convention.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds GO batch separator handling in the statement splitter.
C.contract: New T-SQL splitting capability.

B.label: bug
B.description: StripCommentsFilter removed a comment token without stepping its index back, so the next comment was skipped and an input made only of comments kept '--B;'.
B.contract: strip_comments=True removes all comments; SQL consisting only of comments should format to '' (issue #801).

C.label: bug
C.description: Stripping comments skipped a following comment after removal because the index was not adjusted.
C.contract: strip_comments must remove all comments (issue 801).

B.label: bug
B.description: In the statement splitter, the END of a CASE inside a BEGIN block decremented the BEGIN depth, so a trigger body with several CASE expressions was split before its final END.
B.contract: sqlparse.split must keep a CREATE TRIGGER ... BEGIN ... END block as one statement (issue #784).

C.label: bug
C.description: END of a CASE inside BEGIN block was counted as closing the BEGIN, splitting the statement.
C.contract: Multiple CASE in BEGIN must be one statement (issue 784).

B.label: bug
B.description: Comment grouping greedily absorbed trailing spaces, so stripping a comment also removed the separating space ('SELECT 1/*bar*/ AS foo' became 'SELECT 1AS foo').
B.contract: strip_comments must not merge adjacent tokens or change the SQL (issue #772); the commit also adjusts another expectation as a side effect.

C.label: bug
C.description: Comment grouping consumed trailing whitespace beyond newlines.
C.contract: Grouping was too greedy (issue 772).

B.label: bug
B.description: The PHP output formatter did not escape '$' in the generated double-quoted string, so SQL content triggered PHP variable or expression interpolation.
B.contract: output_format='php' must emit a PHP string literal that reproduces the SQL text exactly (security advisory CVE-2026-112307).

C.label: bug
C.description: PHP output filter did not escape dollar signs, allowing variable interpolation in generated strings.
C.contract: Generated PHP literal must not interpolate; security advisory referenced.

B.label: bug
B.description: The lexer rule tagging a word followed by a period as a Name also fired before a leading-dot float, turning BETWEEN in 'BETWEEN .03 AND .06' into a Name.
B.contract: BETWEEN must stay a keyword and '.03' a number; the Name rule is only meant for 'schema . name' member access (issue #601).

C.label: bug
C.description: Name regex matched a keyword before a leading-dot float, demoting BETWEEN to a Name.
C.contract: Keyword followed by .03 must remain keyword (issue 601).

B.label: bug
B.description: The dollar-quoted string regex required whitespace before '$$', so 'foo =$$bar;SELECT bar$$' was not lexed as a string and was split at the inner semicolon.
B.contract: PostgreSQL allows an operator immediately before a dollar-quoted string; its content must not be split.

C.label: bug
C.description: Dollar-quote regex required whitespace before the opening, so an operator directly before it broke tokenization.
C.contract: Operators may precede dollar-quoted strings in PostgreSQL.

B.label: bug
B.description: MATERIALIZED was missing from the keyword table, so it was lexed as a Name and left unchanged by keyword_case formatting.
B.contract: keyword_case='upper' should normalize every keyword; 'CREATE materialized VIEW' output was inconsistent (issue #752).

C.label: bug
C.description: MATERIALIZED missing from keywords, lexed as Name and skipped by keyword_case.
C.contract: Keywords should be normalized consistently (issue 752).

B.label: bug
B.description: strip_comments also removed optimizer hints (/*+ ... */, --+ ...), which the lexer already tokenizes as distinct Hint types and which change query execution.
B.contract: Hints are semantically significant SQL and are recognized as separate token types; stripping comments must not delete them.

C.label: bug
C.description: strip_comments removed SQL hint comments that must be preserved.
C.contract: Hints such as /*+ ... */ carry semantics and should survive stripping.

B.label: bug
B.description: The lexer split 'ASC/DESC NULLS FIRST/LAST' into separate tokens and typed NULLS FIRST/LAST as a generic keyword instead of an order keyword.
B.contract: An ordering specification such as 'DESC NULLS LAST' is one order keyword, like other multi-word keywords sqlparse lexes as a single token (issue #532); the old test asserted the generic type, hence low confidence.

C.label: bug
C.description: ASC/DESC with NULLS FIRST/LAST was tokenized as separate tokens and with wrong token type.
C.contract: Order keywords should be tokenized as one Order token (issue 532).

B.label: bug
B.description: Deeply nested input made TokenList.flatten exceed the recursion limit and leak a raw RecursionError instead of the library's SQLParseError.
B.contract: The parser should fail on pathological nesting with its own error type that callers can handle; the leaking RecursionError was treated as a denial-of-service issue. Low confidence because only the exception type changes.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: RecursionError is translated to SQLParseError.
C.contract: Deliberate error type change.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: The commit translates recursion-limit failures into SQLParseError while retaining the parsing failure.
T.contract: The packet shows no pre-existing guarantee that recursion exhaustion must raise SQLParseError, and the test checks only the new exception policy.

B.label: feature
B.description: Adds a compact formatting option (and CLI flag) that avoids line breaks in CASE expressions.
B.contract: New option; the test fails only because compact=True did not exist.

C.label: feature
C.description: Adds compact formatting option.
C.contract: New option.

B.label: bug
B.description: group_functions compared the AS token case-sensitively, so a lowercase 'as' in CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT disabled function grouping.
B.contract: SQL keywords are case-insensitive, and the neighbouring CREATE/TABLE checks already use .upper().

C.label: bug
C.description: AS check was case-sensitive so lowercase as disabled function grouping.
C.contract: SQL keywords are case-insensitive.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Exceeding the grouping depth/token limits now raises SQLParseError instead of silently stopping grouping.
B.contract: Deliberate policy change; the tests previously asserted that such inputs format successfully and now expect an exception.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Exceeding grouping limits now raises SQLParseError instead of silently returning.
C.contract: Deliberate DoS-protection policy change with tests updated.

B.label: bug
B.description: ROW_FORMAT was missing from the keyword table, so 'ALTER TABLE mytable ROW_FORMAT=Dynamic' grouped ROW_FORMAT as an alias of the table name.
B.contract: Table options like ENGINE are already keywords and parse correctly; the same statement shape must not misgroup the table name (issue #773).

C.label: bug
C.description: ROW_FORMAT missing from keyword table so it was absorbed as an alias.
C.contract: ROW_FORMAT is a keyword like ENGINE (issue 773).

B.label: bug
B.description: The IF of 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS' was lexed as a control-flow IF, raising the splitter's nesting level so the BEGIN...END block and the next statement were not split.
B.contract: IF EXISTS is a clause, not a control-flow IF; split() should return two statements for the task script (issue #812).

C.label: bug
C.description: IF EXISTS was lexed as control-flow IF, breaking splitting inside BEGIN...END.
C.contract: IF EXISTS is not a control-flow IF (issue 812).

B.label: bug
B.description: get_real_name anchored on the first dot, so for names with three or more parts it returned an intermediate component instead of the last one.
B.contract: get_real_name returns the object name, the component after the last dot (db.schema.tbl.col gives 'col') (issue #332).

C.label: bug
C.description: get_real_name anchored on first dot and returned an intermediate component for 3+ part names.
C.contract: Real name is the final component (issue 332).

B.label: bug
B.description: tomlkit.date() validated the parsed value with isinstance(value, date), which datetime also satisfies, so datetime strings were accepted and returned as a DateTime.
B.contract: date() is meant to create a TOML local date and its own error message states 'date() only accepts date strings'.

C.label: bug
C.description: date() accepted datetime strings since datetime is a date subclass.
C.contract: date() documented to accept only date strings.

B.label: bug
B.description: The compact escape table mapped ESC to the TOML 1.1-only '\e' escape, so dumped strings containing ESC could not be read by TOML 1.0 parsers such as tomllib.
B.contract: tomlkit presents itself as a TOML 1.0.0-compliant library, so its serialized output must be valid TOML 1.0 (\u001b).

C.label: bug
C.description: ESC was written as the TOML 1.1-only \e escape.
C.contract: Output should be valid TOML 1.0.

B.label: bug
B.description: StringType treated '\r' as an allowed multiline character, so a lone carriage return was neither escaped in multiline basic strings nor rejected in multiline literal strings, producing invalid TOML.
B.contract: TOML 1.0 allows only LF or CRLF line endings inside multiline strings and treats a lone CR as a control character that must be escaped; tomlkit.string() must not emit invalid TOML.

C.label: bug
C.description: Lone carriage returns were allowed unescaped in multiline strings.
C.contract: TOML requires control chars to be escaped; only LF or CRLF are line endings.

B.label: bug
B.description: Bool.__eq__ returned NotImplemented for any non-bool operand, including another Bool item, so item(True) == item(True) was False and arrays of booleans parsed from identical text compared unequal.
B.contract: TOML items compare by value like their Python counterparts, and equality must be reflexive for equal values.

C.label: bug
C.description: Bool items did not compare equal to other Bool items.
C.contract: Equal booleans should compare equal.

B.label: bug
B.description: When a key was appended to a parsed inline table, the deferred separator was inserted as a bare ',' with no following space, so 'a = {x = 1, y = 2}' became 'a = {x = 1, y = 2,z = 3}'.
B.contract: tomlkit preserves formatting and otherwise renders inline-table entries separated by ', '; the output stayed valid TOML, so the fault is cosmetic and the call is close to a formatting-policy change.

C.label: bug
C.description: Appended inline table key used a bare comma without the surrounding spacing convention.
C.contract: Appending should keep the table consistently spaced.

B.label: bug
B.description: _validate_table_candidate raised 'Redefinition of an existing table' for any dotted key that hit an existing table, even when that table was an implicit super-table, so '[a.b.c]\n[a]\nb.z = 1' was rejected.
B.contract: The document is valid TOML (tomllib accepts it): no table is defined twice, a.b only gains a key, so the parser must accept and round-trip it.

C.label: bug
C.description: A valid out-of-order super-table extended by a dotted key was rejected as a redefinition.
C.contract: Valid TOML accepted by tomllib must parse.

B.label: bug
B.description: item() called a custom encoder with both _parent and _sort_keys whenever it declared _parent (or **kwargs), and with neither otherwise, so encoders accepting only one of them crashed with an unexpected-keyword TypeError or silently missed the context.
B.contract: Custom encoders may optionally accept the _parent and _sort_keys context keywords; an encoder declaring only _parent, only _sort_keys, or naming its value parameter _parent is valid and must be called with arguments it accepts.

C.label: bug
C.description: Custom encoders were passed context kwargs they do not accept.
C.contract: Encoders should receive only supported parameters.

B.label: bug
B.description: Table.append copied the header indent onto the stored item via _item.trivia, but when the key had been split out of order the lookup returned an OutOfOrderTableProxy without trivia, raising AttributeError (surfacing as ParseError).
B.contract: Documents such as ' [a.b.c.d]\n[a.b.c]' are valid TOML and must parse and round-trip.

C.label: bug
C.description: Table.append accessed trivia on an OutOfOrderTableProxy, raising AttributeError.
C.contract: Parsing indented header out-of-order tables must work (issue 663).

B.label: bug
B.description: DateTime.__sub__ rebuilt a plain datetime from its fields without passing fold before subtracting an aware datetime, so subtracting from a folded local time gave a timedelta off by the fold offset.
B.contract: tomlkit DateTime items are meant to behave like datetime: item(value) - other must equal value - other.

C.label: bug
C.description: DateTime subtraction rebuilt the value without fold.
C.contract: Fold must be preserved in arithmetic.

B.label: bug
B.description: The number parser matched special float literals case-insensitively, so invalid TOML such as 'v = Inf' or 'v = NaN' was accepted instead of raising ParseError.
B.contract: TOML 1.0.0, with which tomlkit claims compliance, allows only lowercase inf and nan, so other spellings are invalid documents.

C.label: bug
C.description: Parser accepted non-lowercase INF/NAN float literals.
C.contract: TOML spec requires lowercase inf and nan.

B.label: bug
B.description: merge_dicts replaced an existing list with the next fragment's list, so when an array of tables was split by unrelated tables, doc.value and unwrap() kept only the last fragment's elements.
B.contract: An array of tables whose [[...]] headers are separated by other tables is valid TOML, and unwrap()/value must contain every element (as_string already round-tripped them).

C.label: bug
C.description: merge_dicts replaced instead of extending split arrays of tables, losing entries.
C.contract: Document values must preserve all array-of-table parts.

B.label: bug
B.description: Float._new prefixed '+' whenever the source had an explicit sign and result >= 0, and -0.0 >= 0 is true, so an arithmetic result of -0.0 was written as '+-0.0', which tomlkit's own parser rejects.
B.contract: Arithmetic on document values must keep as_string() valid TOML; '-1.5 * 0' should render as '-0.0'.

C.label: bug
C.description: Negative zero results received an extra plus sign, producing +-0.0.
C.contract: Output must be valid TOML parseable by tomlkit.

B.label: bug
B.description: InlineTable._render_dotted emitted nothing when every key under a dotted prefix had been deleted, so the inline table rendered an empty slot between separators (e.g. 'a = {x = 1, , y = 2}').
B.contract: Deleting a key through the document API must keep as_string() valid, round-trippable TOML that matches the document's contents (an empty table b).

C.label: bug
C.description: Removing the last key under a dotted prefix in an inline table left an empty slot producing invalid TOML.
C.contract: Output must remain valid TOML.

B.label: bug
B.description: Array.as_string for a single-line array appended ']' directly after the last rendered element, so when that element was a trailing comment added via add_line(comment=...) the bracket landed inside the comment and the output no longer parsed.
B.contract: Arrays built through the public API must render to TOML that parses back to the same value (GH #580).

C.label: bug
C.description: Single-line array rendering put the closing bracket on a trailing comment line, producing unparseable output.
C.contract: Output must round-trip (GH 580).

B.label: bug
B.description: DateTime.unwrap and Time.unwrap rebuilt the stdlib value without passing fold, so a folded (repeated) local time unwrapped to the other occurrence and its timestamp/offset was an hour off.
B.contract: unwrap() must return a plain datetime/time equal in meaning to the wrapped value; fold is part of that value.

C.label: bug
C.description: unwrap() on DateTime and Time dropped fold.
C.contract: Unwrapped value must preserve fold.

B.label: bug
B.description: Array.__delitem__ computed the removed render slots as range(key.start or 0, key.stop or length, key.step or 1), so a stop of 0 was treated as the end and negative bounds were not normalised, making as_string() drift from the list contents (e.g. del a[:0] rendered '[]').
B.contract: Array behaves like a list, and its rendered output must stay consistent with its contents after slice deletion.

C.label: bug
C.description: Array slice deletion computed indices ignoring slice defaults and negatives, corrupting the render.
C.contract: Deleting a slice must match list semantics.

B.label: bug
B.description: tomlkit.key_value() parsed one pair and never checked that the input was fully consumed, so trailing text such as 'foo = 12 junk' was silently discarded instead of raising.
B.contract: TOML requires a newline or EOF after a key/value pair and parse() rejects the same inputs; value() already guarded against trailing input.

C.label: bug
C.description: key_value() silently discarded trailing characters after the pair.
C.contract: TOML requires newline or EOF after a pair, enforced by parse().

B.label: bug
B.description: item() sorted dict-valued keys last for every table built from a list, including inline tables, so under the default sort_keys=False an inline table's keys were silently reordered.
B.contract: With sort_keys=False insertion order is kept (as the dict branch already did); the dicts-last rule is only needed for [[table]] headers, and issue #546 reports the reordering.

C.label: bug
C.description: item() sorted dict-valued keys last even for inline tables, reordering keys.
C.contract: Insertion order must be preserved by default (issue 546).

B.label: bug
B.description: OutOfOrderTableProxy.__setitem__ stored a new key in one of the underlying tables without recording it in _tables_map, so a later delete/pop raised NonExistentKey and re-assigning the key appended a duplicate that broke re-parsing.
B.contract: A key added through the dict-like proxy must be removable and replaceable like any other key, and the document must stay valid TOML.

C.label: bug
C.description: New keys set on an out-of-order table proxy were not tracked, so deletion raised NonExistentKey.
C.contract: Keys set on the proxy must be removable.

B.label: bug
B.description: Source._to_linecol advanced its running offset by len(line) + 1 for every line, assuming a one-character terminator, so CRLF and mixed line endings made parse errors report the wrong line and column.
B.contract: Parse errors must report the actual position of the offending character, which does not depend on the document's line-ending style.

C.label: bug
C.description: Line and column in errors were off for CRLF and mixed line endings.
C.contract: Error positions should be correct for any line ending.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Array insertion updates the index map incrementally for tail appends of regular values and only rebuilds it in the other cases.
B.contract: This is a performance optimisation; the failing test only asserts that _reindex is not called, and the array's observable contents and formatting were already correct.

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: Array append avoids a full reindex as a performance optimization.
C.contract: Performance refactor; test asserts no reindexing.

B.label: bug
B.description: Float.__round__ defaulted ndigits to 0 and always returned a Float, so round(item(2.5)) gave the float 2.0 instead of an integer and non-finite values did not raise OverflowError/ValueError.
B.contract: tomlkit's Float subclasses float and is meant to behave like one; Python's round(x) without ndigits returns an int and raises for inf/nan.

C.label: bug
C.description: Float.__round__ without digits returned a Float rather than an Integer and did not raise for non-finite.
C.contract: round(x) must return an int like built-in float.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: Assigning a plain str to a key whose current value is a single-line literal string keeps the literal quote style when possible, where the replacement was rendered with the default basic-string style.
B.contract: Replacement values were converted with the default item() formatting, the same as for every other string type (which the commit keeps); inheriting the previous quote style is a new formatting policy, not a repaired guarantee.

C.label: bug
C.description: Replacing a literal string value in a table converted it to a basic string, losing style.
C.contract: Replacing a value should preserve the literal quote style.

T.label: behavior_change
T.description: Changes replacement-string serialization to inherit existing single-line literal quoting when the new value permits it.
T.contract: The failures demonstrate a quoting-style difference rather than incorrect values or invalid TOML; the packet provides no prior guarantee of quote inheritance, and the tests retain default quoting for arrays and other string styles.

B.label: bug
B.description: The _new helpers of Integer, Float, String, DateTime, Date and Time passed the original item's Trivia object to the arithmetic result, so editing the result's comment or indent rewrote the line still stored in the document.
B.contract: An arithmetic result is a new value and must not alias the source item's state; Table and InlineTable copies already copied their trivia.

C.label: bug
C.description: Arithmetic results shared the original item's Trivia, so editing the result mutated the document.
C.contract: Results must not alias the original's trivia.

B.label: feature
B.description: tomlkit.integer() treats string input as a TOML integer literal: it validates it against the TOML 1.0 grammar, accepts hex/octal/binary forms and keeps the original text (including grouping underscores) as the item's raw value.
B.contract: integer(str) was implemented as item(int(raw)), i.e. a plain int conversion with no promise to keep the text or accept prefixed literals; preserving raw text, adding prefixed forms and rejecting strings int() accepted are new string-input semantics.

C.label: bug
C.description: api.integer discarded underscores by normalizing the raw string through int().
C.contract: Valid TOML integers with underscores should be preserved verbatim.

T.label: bug
T.description: Constructing integer items through item(int(raw)) discarded literal formatting and rejected valid nondecimal TOML integer strings.
T.contract: The existing integer API promises construction from strings, and the commit and tests demonstrate valid TOML integer literals already supported by parsing that the constructor rejected or normalized.

B.label: bug
B.description: isiterable checked only hasattr(x, '__iter__'), misclassifying objects iterable via __getitem__ and objects that set __iter__ = None.
B.contract: Python's iteration protocol (iter()) defines iterability; reverting the earlier 'faster' change restores the previously correct behaviour.

C.label: bug
C.description: isiterable used hasattr __iter__ and returned False for __getitem__-only iterables.
C.contract: Python iter() protocol includes __getitem__ objects.

B.label: behavior_change
B.description: partition_all now raises LookupError when a sequence's __len__ disagrees with its contents instead of yielding incorrect chunks.
B.contract: The fault lies in the caller's iterable with an invalid __len__; this adds a new validation policy (#602).

C.label: behavior_change
C.description: partition_all now raises LookupError when a sequence reports an inconsistent length.
C.contract: Deliberate new validation for invalid iterables instead of silent bad output.

B.label: bug
B.description: interpose called next() on the pipeline unconditionally, so an empty sequence raised StopIteration instead of yielding nothing.
B.contract: interpose of an empty sequence should be an empty iterator; leaking StopIteration is a crash on valid input (#635).

C.label: bug
C.description: interpose on an empty sequence raised StopIteration.
C.contract: interpose of empty sequence should be empty.
